en.editorNote: For the person who opens social media and instantly thinks 'everyone's crushing it and I'm stuck.' This hands the pace back to them. Send to a friend who's anxious and always measuring against others.
variations: There's no rule about where you should be by a certain age. Your timezone is yours alone.
Slow isn't behind. It just means you're taking every step seriously.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'the only way out is through' resilience theme; original writing on being present with pain

zh-tw.content:
難過的時候不用假裝沒事，
你可以哭一場，然後我還是會在這裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些習慣在別人面前撐住、怕拖累人的人。給他們一個可以放下的地方。適合傳給那種總說「不想麻煩你」的朋友。
variations: 你不用等到好起來才值得被陪，現在這樣也可以。
想哭就哭吧，我不會走，也不會催你趕快好。

en.content:
When it hurts, you don't have to pretend you're fine.
Go ahead and cry — and I'll still be right here.
en.editorNote: For the person who holds it together in front of everyone, afraid of being a burden. This gives them somewhere to put it down. Send to a friend who's always saying 'I don't want to bother you.'
variations: You don't have to be okay before you deserve company. Right now, like this, is fine too.
Cry if you need to. I won't leave, and I won't rush you to feel better.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '允許自己偶爾停滯不前，四季都有枯榮' seasonal-rest theme; original writing on winter/dormancy metaphor

zh-tw.content:
允許自己偶爾停在原地吧。
樹到冬天也會落葉，不是它壞掉了，只是在等下一個春天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一沒進度就開始責備自己的人。停滯不是退步，是季節。適合傳給最近覺得「怎麼別人都在往前，只有我卡住」的朋友。
variations: 沒有一直往前才叫活著，會停會慢也是。
你不是停下來了，你是在等自己準備好。

en.content:
Let yourself stay still sometimes.
Trees drop their leaves in winter too — they're not broken, they're just waiting for spring.
en.editorNote: For the person who starts blaming themselves the moment progress stalls. Being stuck isn't going backward — it's a season. Send to a friend who feels like everyone else is moving forward but them.
variations: Living isn't only moving forward. Pausing and slowing down count too.
You didn't stop. You're just waiting until you're ready.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'healing does not rush; it lingers until you feel safe' theme; original writing on healing at its own pace

zh-tw.content:
好起來是沒有進度條的。
它不會照你排的時間走，但它一直在走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種會給自己設「多久要好起來」期限的人。復原沒有時間表，卡著不代表沒在動。適合傳給對自己失去耐性的朋友。
variations: 你以為原地踏步，其實只是進度太安靜，你沒聽見而已。
傷口癒合不會問你趕不趕時間，它有自己的節奏。

en.content:
Healing doesn't come with a progress bar.
It won't follow your schedule — but it's still moving.
en.editorNote: For the person who sets themselves a deadline to 'be better by.' Recovery has no timetable, and feeling stuck doesn't mean nothing's happening. Send to a friend who's lost patience with themselves.
variations: You think you're standing still, but the progress is just quiet — you didn't hear it.
A wound doesn't care whether you're in a hurry. It heals at its own pace.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'some days healing looks like courage, other days it looks like rest' theme; original writing reframing rest as strength

zh-tw.content:
有些日子，撐下去很勇敢。
有些日子，願意休息也很勇敢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種只把「硬撐」當作堅強的人。停下來需要更大的勇氣。適合傳給覺得休息就是輸的朋友，或提醒累到不行的自己。
variations: 願意承認自己需要休息，其實比咬牙硬撐更難。
今天沒有崩潰就已經很棒了，剩下的明天再說。

en.content:
Some days, holding on is brave.
Other days, letting yourself rest is just as brave.
en.editorNote: For the person who only counts 'pushing through' as strength. Stopping takes more courage. Send to a friend who feels like resting means losing — or remind your own worn-out self.
variations: Admitting you need rest is actually harder than gritting your teeth and pushing on.
Not falling apart today is already enough. The rest can wait for tomorrow.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '日子是慢慢過的，好起來也是' pacing theme; original writing on things quietly getting better

zh-tw.content:
日子是一天一天過的，
好起來也是。不用一次全部好，能好一點點就已經很了不起了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種急著想「立刻全部變好」的人。給他們一個把標準放低的許可。適合傳給對現況焦慮、想趕快翻頁的朋友。
variations: 今天比昨天多笑一次，就已經是在往好的方向走了。
不用一次好起來，慢慢好，也是好。

en.content:
Days pass one at a time,
and so does getting better. You don't have to be all okay at once — even a little better is a big deal.
en.editorNote: For the person rushing to 'be completely fine right now.' This gives them permission to lower the bar. Send to a friend who's anxious about where they are and desperate to turn the page.
variations: One more laugh today than yesterday means you're already heading the right way.
You don't have to heal all at once. Slowly is still healing.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'healing doesn't always look like progress' theme; original writing on quiet, non-visible healing

zh-tw.content:
好起來，不一定看得出來。
有時候它長得就像：今天有好好吃飯、有洗澡、有多睡一點。這些也算。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給覺得自己「沒有在進步」而更焦慮的人。把康復的標準拉回日常小事。適合傳給對自己很嚴格、老是嫌自己不夠好的朋友。
variations: 有些進步很安靜，安靜到連你自己都沒發現。
把今天過完，就已經是一種本事了。

en.content:
Getting better doesn't always show.
Sometimes it looks like: you ate today, you showered, you slept a little longer. That counts too.
en.editorNote: For the person who gets more anxious because they feel like they're 'not improving.' Pulls the bar back down to everyday things. Send to a friend who's hard on themselves and never thinks they're doing enough.
variations: Some progress is quiet — so quiet even you don't notice it.
Just making it through today is already something.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'gentleness is not weakness' theme; original rewrite on softness as strength

zh-tw.content:
對自己溫柔一點，
不是軟弱。能一直對自己兇的人才不厲害，願意放過自己的人才勇敢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種對別人很好、對自己特別狠的人。適合傳給總是先檢討自己、捨不得對自己說一句好話的朋友。
variations: 你對全世界都很好，也記得留一點溫柔給自己。
放過自己，不是認輸，是懂事了。

en.content:
Being gentle with yourself
isn't weak. Anyone can be hard on themselves — it takes real courage to let yourself off the hook.
en.editorNote: For the person who's kind to everyone but brutal to themselves. Send to a friend who always blames themselves first and can't bring themselves to say one nice thing about who they are.
variations: You're good to the whole world — save a little softness for yourself too.
Letting yourself off the hook isn't giving up. It's finally getting it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '慢慢來的日子就是冬天，你不是在枯萎而是在扎根' rooting metaphor; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
那些看起來停在原地的日子，
其實你不是在枯萎，是在往下扎根。冬天沒有花，不代表樹死了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給正在低潮、覺得自己「什麼都沒進展」的人。用季節的比喻讓停滯變得可以被接受。適合傳給撐得很累、快要對自己失望的朋友。
variations: 看起來停下來的時候，你可能正在偷偷長根。
沒開花的季節，也是在為下一次盛開存力氣。

en.content:
Those days you feel stuck in place —
you're not withering, you're growing roots. A tree with no flowers in winter isn't a dead tree.
en.editorNote: For the person in a slump who feels like 'nothing is moving.' Uses a seasonal metaphor to make standing still feel okay. Send to a friend who's worn out and on the edge of giving up on themselves.
variations: When it looks like you've stopped, you might quietly be putting down roots.
The season without blossoms is still storing up strength for the next one.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'healing does not rush; it lingers until you feel safe' theme; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
好起來這件事，是不能催的。
它會等你覺得安全了，才慢慢靠過來。你只要先讓自己安心，剩下的它會自己來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給急著想「趕快好」的人。提醒他們療癒有自己的節奏，急也沒用。適合傳給對復原進度焦慮、想快點翻篇的朋友。
variations: 不用逼自己趕快沒事，它會在你放鬆的時候自己出現。
先讓自己安心，好起來就會慢慢跟上。

en.content:
Getting better can't be rushed.
It waits until you feel safe, then slowly comes closer. Your only job is to feel okay first — the rest finds its own way in.
en.editorNote: For the person desperate to 'hurry up and heal.' Reminds them that healing keeps its own pace, and rushing won't help. Send to a friend anxious about their recovery who just wants to turn the page.
variations: You don't have to force yourself to be fine — it shows up when you finally relax.
Let yourself feel safe first, and getting better will slowly catch up.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'be gentle with yourself, rest is part of repair'; original rewrite reframing rest as necessary healing

zh-tw.content:
休息不是療癒的空檔，休息本身就是療癒的一部分。
你不是在浪費時間，你是在把自己修好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些覺得「躺著就是罪惡」的人。把休息重新定義成修復的必要工序，而不是偷懶。適合傳給忙到忘記怎麼停下來的朋友。
variations: 停下來不是暫停復原，停下來就是復原的一步。
你不是在耍廢，你是在讓自己慢慢長回來。

en.content:
Rest isn't a gap in your healing — rest is the healing.
You're not wasting time. You're putting yourself back together.
en.editorNote: For the person who feels guilty just lying down. Reframes rest as a required part of repair, not laziness. Send to a friend so busy they've forgotten how to stop.
variations: Slowing down doesn't pause your recovery — it is your recovery.
You're not being lazy. You're letting yourself grow back.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you do not have to explain why your heart is tired'; original rewrite on permission to feel without justifying

zh-tw.content:
你不用解釋為什麼心會累。
累了就是累了，不需要一個夠格的理由。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種難過還要先自我審查「我有資格難過嗎」的人。告訴他情緒不需要通過審核才成立。適合傳給總覺得「別人更慘所以我不該抱怨」的朋友。
variations: 心累不用附上原因，它本來就有權利存在。
不是要慘到某個程度，你才可以說你不好。

en.content:
You don't owe anyone an explanation for why your heart is tired.
Tired is tired. It doesn't need a good enough reason.
en.editorNote: For the person who interrogates their own sadness — 'am I even allowed to feel this?' Reminds them emotions don't need to pass an audit to be valid. Send to a friend who thinks 'others have it worse, so I can't complain.'
variations: A tired heart needs no footnote. It's allowed to exist as it is.
You don't have to hit some threshold of awful before you're allowed to say you're not okay.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Mandy Hale theme 'growth is painful, but staying stuck where you don't belong is more painful'; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
改變會痛，這是真的。
但你有沒有想過，一直待在讓你慢慢枯掉的地方，其實更痛，只是那種痛你已經習慣了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種明明不快樂、卻因為害怕改變而不敢動的人。提醒他「熟悉的痛」也是痛，不是安全。適合傳給卡在爛工作或爛關係裡的朋友。
variations: 待在不對的地方久了，你會以為那種鈍鈍的痛是正常的。它不是。
離開會痛一陣子，留下來會痛一輩子。

en.content:
Change hurts — that's true.
But staying somewhere that's slowly wearing you down hurts more. You've just gotten used to that kind of pain.
en.editorNote: For the person who's clearly unhappy but too scared of change to move. Reminds them that 'familiar pain' is still pain, not safety. Send to a friend stuck in a bad job or relationship.
variations: Stay somewhere wrong long enough and you start thinking the dull ache is normal. It isn't.
Leaving hurts for a while. Staying hurts for a lifetime.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Kristin Neff theme 'a moment of self-compassion can change your day, a string of them your life'; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
對自己溫柔一下下，就能救回一整天的心情。
這種溫柔累積起來，甚至能慢慢改變你往後的日子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種對別人很寬容、對自己卻很嚴苛的人。提醒他自我善待不是奢侈，是可以練習、也真的有用的小事。適合貼在鏡子上，或傳給常常自責的朋友。
variations: 一個對自己好一點的瞬間，就足以扭轉今天。
你對自己的溫柔不會白費，它會慢慢改寫你的人生。

en.content:
One small moment of being kind to yourself can rescue a whole day.
String enough of those moments together and they can change the shape of your life.
en.editorNote: For the person who's endlessly forgiving of others but brutal on themselves. Reminds them self-kindness isn't a luxury — it's a small, practiceable thing that actually works. Stick it on a mirror, or send to a friend who's always beating themselves up.
variations: A single moment of self-compassion is enough to turn a day around.
The gentleness you give yourself is never wasted — it quietly rewrites your life.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '生活本來就有很多不完美，練習多看身邊的美好' theme; original rewrite on imperfection

zh-tw.content:
生活本來就不會事事完美，
與其盯著缺口難過，不如練習多看一眼旁邊還好好的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一有一件事出錯，就覺得整天都毀了的人。提醒他不完美是常態，好的部分也一直都在，只是需要被看見。適合傳給容易鑽牛角尖的朋友。
variations: 不完美不是壞掉，是生活本來的樣子。
別讓一個缺口，遮住你其實過得還不錯的那一大片。

en.content:
Life was never going to be perfect at everything.
Instead of staring at the gap and aching, practice glancing at the parts that are still okay.
en.editorNote: For the person who feels the whole day is ruined the moment one thing goes wrong. Reminds them imperfection is the norm, and the good parts are still there — they just need to be noticed. Send to a friend who tends to spiral over small things.
variations: Imperfect doesn't mean broken. It's just what life actually looks like.
Don't let one gap hide the whole wide stretch of life that's going just fine.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '放過自己' healing theme; original rewrite on forgiving yourself

zh-tw.content:
你已經為了那件事，罰自己夠久了。
放過自己，不是原諒錯，是不想再讓過去偷走現在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一件小事就內疚很久、反覆責怪自己的人。提醒他懲罰自己並不會讓事情變好，只會讓現在也一起壞掉。適合傳給對自己特別嚴苛的朋友。
variations: 你不欠自己一輩子的愧疚，該放下的時候就放下吧。
檢討過就好，別把同一件事拿出來，一遍又一遍地判自己有罪。

en.content:
You've punished yourself over that long enough.
Letting yourself off the hook isn't excusing the mistake — it's refusing to let the past keep stealing your present.
en.editorNote: For the person who feels guilty for ages over something small and keeps replaying the blame. A reminder that punishing yourself doesn't fix anything — it just ruins the present too. Send to a friend who's especially hard on themselves.
variations: You don't owe yourself a lifetime of guilt. When it's time to put it down, put it down.
You've reviewed it. Stop pulling the same thing back out to find yourself guilty all over again.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Kristin Neff's common-humanity concept; original rewrite on it being okay to be imperfect

zh-tw.content:
你不用完美才值得被喜歡。
會累、會出錯、會有做不到的時候，這不是你的缺陷，這只是你是個人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種覺得「一定要做到最好，不然就沒價值」的人。提醒他不完美是所有人的共同點，不是他一個人的問題。適合傳給對自己要求很高、卻總覺得不夠好的朋友。
variations: 沒有人是完整無缺的，你也不需要當那個例外。
會犯錯不代表你不好，只代表你跟每個人一樣，是真的人。

en.content:
You don't have to be perfect to deserve being liked.
Getting tired, making mistakes, having things you can't do — that's not a flaw in you. That's just you being human.
en.editorNote: For the person who feels they have to be the best or they have no worth. A reminder that imperfection is something everyone shares — it's not their personal defect. Send to a friend who holds themselves to impossibly high standards yet never feels good enough.
variations: Nobody is flawless, and you don't have to be the exception.
Making mistakes doesn't mean you're bad. It means you're a real person, like everyone else.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '時間最無情也最溫柔' healing theme; original rewrite on time and healing

zh-tw.content:
時間不會替你把傷抹掉，
但它會慢慢讓你想起的時候，不再那麼痛。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種急著想「趕快好起來」卻好不了的人。提醒他復原不是把事情忘掉，而是它慢慢變得可以承受。適合傳給正在走過失去或分開的朋友。
variations: 傷口不是消失了，是你變得比它強了一點。
現在覺得撐不過去很正常，時間會證明你其實可以。

en.content:
Time won't erase the wound for you.
But slowly, it makes remembering hurt a little less.
en.editorNote: For the person rushing to 'just get over it' who can't. A reminder that healing isn't forgetting — it's the thing slowly becoming bearable. Send to a friend making their way through a loss or a breakup.
variations: The wound didn't vanish. You just grew a little stronger than it.
Feeling like you can't make it through is normal right now. Time will prove that you can.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you do not have to be fully healed to move forward'; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
你不用等到完全好起來，才有資格往前走。
帶著還沒好的傷繼續生活，本身就是一種勇敢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種覺得「我還這麼糟，憑什麼過得好」的人。提醒他復原和生活可以同時進行，不必等傷全好才開始。適合傳給遲遲不敢往前、卡在原地的朋友。
variations: 傷還在沒關係，你可以一邊痛、一邊前進。
不是等好了才出發，是走著走著就慢慢好了。

en.content:
You don't have to be fully healed before you're allowed to move forward.
Living while you're still hurting is its own kind of brave.
en.editorNote: For the person who thinks 'I'm still such a mess, what right do I have to be okay.' A reminder that healing and living can happen at the same time. Send to a friend who's stuck in place, too afraid to move on.
variations: It's okay that the wound is still there. You can hurt and move forward at the same time.
You don't wait until you're healed to set out. You heal a little from the walking.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Christopher Germer 'a moment of self-compassion can change your entire day'; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
對自己溫柔一次，可能只改變了一個下午；
但一次又一次地溫柔，會慢慢改變你看自己的方式。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種對別人很好、對自己特別苛刻的人。提醒他自我疼惜不是一次到位，而是靠日常一點一滴累積出來的。適合傳給總是先罵自己一頓的完美主義朋友。
variations: 你怎麼對自己說話，久了就會變成你怎麼看自己。
別急著要一次原諒自己，先從這個當下對自己好一點開始。

en.content:
Being kind to yourself once might only change an afternoon.
Being kind to yourself again and again slowly changes how you see yourself.
en.editorNote: For the person who's generous with everyone but brutal with themselves. A reminder that self-compassion isn't a one-time fix — it's built up in small daily doses. Send to a perfectionist friend who always scolds themselves first.
variations: The way you talk to yourself becomes, over time, the way you see yourself.
Don't rush to forgive yourself all at once. Just start by being a little kinder in this moment.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '你會怎麼照顧五歲的自己，就怎麼照顧現在的你'; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
如果五歲的你跌倒了在哭，你不會罵他沒用，
你會蹲下來抱抱他。現在的你，也值得這樣被對待。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一犯錯就狠狠責備自己的人。用「小時候的自己」當視角，讓他重新學會對現在的自己溫柔。適合傳給正在自責、覺得都是自己不好的朋友。
variations: 你對別人的小孩都比對自己好，該換你抱抱自己了。
犯錯的時候，先別急著檢討，先問問自己還好嗎。

en.content:
If your five-year-old self fell and cried, you wouldn't call them useless —
you'd crouch down and hold them. You deserve to be treated that way now, too.
en.editorNote: For the person who tears into themselves the moment they slip up. Uses the 'younger self' lens to help them relearn gentleness toward who they are now. Send to a friend drowning in self-blame, sure it's all their fault.
variations: You're kinder to other people's kids than to yourself. It's your turn to hold yourself.
When you mess up, don't rush to the post-mortem. First ask yourself if you're okay.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '真正的放下並不是丟掉，而是能把曾經好好放在記憶裡'; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
放下不是把那個人從記憶裡刪掉，
是你終於可以想起他，卻不再想回頭。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種以為「還會想起就代表沒放下」而自責的人。提醒他放下不是失憶，而是心境變了。適合傳給走過一段感情、還在懷疑自己有沒有真的放下的朋友。
variations: 會想起是正常的，重點是你已經不想回去了。
放下不是假裝沒發生過，是把它好好收進過去。

en.content:
Letting go isn't deleting someone from your memory.
It's finally being able to remember them without wanting to go back.
en.editorNote: For the person who beats themselves up thinking 'if I still remember, I mustn't have let go.' A reminder that letting go isn't amnesia — it's a shift in where you stand. Send to a friend past a relationship who's still doubting whether they've truly moved on.
variations: Remembering is normal. What matters is that you no longer want to return.
Letting go isn't pretending it never happened. It's tucking it neatly into the past.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'healing is an art; it takes time, practice, and patience' — Maza-Dohta; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
好起來這件事，不會照你排的進度表走。
它會用它自己的速度，慢慢把你接住。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種急著「我已經難過夠久了，怎麼還沒好」的人。提醒他復原沒有標準工期，允許自己慢一點。適合傳給對自己失去耐心、覺得拖太久的朋友。
variations: 你沒有進度落後，療傷本來就沒有時間表。
別催自己快點好，好起來也需要練習跟耐心。

en.content:
Getting better won't follow the timeline you drew up for it.
It heals you at its own pace, slowly catching you as you fall.
en.editorNote: For the person anxiously asking 'I've been sad long enough, why am I not over it.' A reminder that healing has no standard schedule — give yourself permission to be slow. Send to a friend who's lost patience with themselves for 'taking too long.'
variations: You're not behind. Healing never came with a deadline.
Stop rushing yourself to be okay. Getting better takes practice and patience too.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '不需要每天過得轟轟烈烈，收集幾個微小的快樂就足夠'; original rewrite on collecting small joys

zh-tw.content:
日子不用過得轟轟烈烈，
每天撿到幾個小小的開心，就夠撐過一整天了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種覺得「生活好像沒什麼意義」的人。提醒他快樂不一定要很大，一杯熱的、一句晚安都算。適合傳給最近覺得每天都很平淡、有點提不起勁的朋友。
variations: 不必等大事發生才快樂，小確幸攢一攢也能過得下去。
今天有沒有哪個瞬間讓你嘴角動了一下？那就是今天的收穫。

en.content:
Your days don't have to be spectacular.
Just collect a few tiny joys each day — that's enough to carry you through.
en.editorNote: For people who feel like life has gotten flat and pointless. A reminder that happiness doesn't have to be big — a warm drink, a goodnight text, they all count. Send to a friend whose days have felt gray and low-energy lately.
variations: You don't have to wait for something huge to feel happy. Small good moments add up.
Was there one moment today that tugged your mouth into a smile? That's today's harvest.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '情緒生病跟感冒一樣正常，清晨的陽光遲早會灑進來'; original rewrite on emotions as illness

zh-tw.content:
情緒生病，跟感冒一樣正常。
就算現在覺得被關在黑暗裡，早晨的光，遲早會照進來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種因為「心情不好」而覺得自己很糟糕的人。提醒他情緒低落不是缺陷，是會過去的狀態。適合傳給正在低潮、覺得自己好不起來的朋友。
variations: 心也會感冒，這不是你的錯，休息一下就會好。
現在很暗沒關係，天亮不需要你做什麼，它自己會來。

en.content:
Emotions getting sick is as normal as catching a cold.
Even if it feels like you're locked in the dark right now, the morning light will find its way in.
en.editorNote: For people who feel like something's wrong with them just because they're feeling down. A reminder that low moods aren't a defect — they're a state that passes. Send to a friend in a slump who's convinced they'll never feel better.
variations: Your heart can catch a cold too. It's not your fault — rest and it'll pass.
It's dark right now, and that's okay. Dawn doesn't need you to do anything — it comes on its own.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you can be struggling and still be worthy of love and patience'; original rewrite on worthiness while struggling

zh-tw.content:
你可以一邊撐得很辛苦，
一邊還是值得被好好對待、被耐心等待。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種覺得「等我好起來才配被愛」的人。提醒他值得被溫柔對待不需要先變好，現在的你就已經夠格。適合傳給正在硬撐、卻覺得自己是負擔的朋友。
variations: 不用等你狀態好了才值得被愛，你現在這樣就值得。
辛苦跟值得被珍惜，這兩件事可以同時成立。

en.content:
You can be barely holding it together
and still deserve to be treated well, and waited for with patience.
en.editorNote: For people who feel they have to get better before they're worthy of love. A reminder that being treated gently isn't something you earn by fixing yourself first — you already qualify, exactly as you are. Send to a friend who's struggling but feels like a burden.
variations: You don't have to wait until you're okay to deserve love. You deserve it right now.
Struggling and being worth cherishing can both be true at the same time.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the idea that burnout happens when you ignore the whispers and wait for the screams; fully rewritten

zh-tw.content:
身體一開始都是小小聲地提醒你，
是你一直說「再撐一下」，
它才只好用生病來大聲講。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種肩頸痛了兩個月、睡不好還在加班的工作狂朋友。重點不是罵他不愛惜自己，而是讓他發現那些被忽略的小訊號其實一直都在。適合在對方喊累卻又說「還好啦」的時候傳過去。
variations: 在你真的倒下之前，身體其實提醒過你很多次了。
那些你覺得「還可以忍」的小不舒服，都是提醒，不是雜訊。

en.content:
Your body starts by whispering.
You keep saying "just a little longer,"
so eventually it has to shout.
en.editorNote: For the friend who's had shoulder pain for two months and is still working late. The point isn't to scold them for neglecting themselves, but to help them notice the small signals that were there all along. Good to send when someone says they're exhausted and then immediately adds "but I'm fine."
variations: Long before you break down, your body tried to tell you — quietly, more than once.
The little aches you decided you could tolerate were messages, not noise.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'feeling overwhelmed isn't failure, it's feedback'; original rewrite

zh-tw.content:
覺得快撐不住，不代表你失敗了，
那只是在告訴你：
你現在扛的份量，本來就超過一個人的量。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一崩潰就先怪自己「怎麼這麼弱」的人。把「我不行」重新翻譯成「這件事太重」，責任就從人身上移回事情上。適合朋友忙到哭出來、卻還在道歉的時候。
variations: 不是你太弱，是那個重量本來就不該一個人扛。
撐不住是訊息，不是判決。

en.content:
Feeling like you can't cope isn't failure.
It's information —
what you're carrying was never a one-person load.
en.editorNote: For people whose first move in a breakdown is to call themselves weak. It re-translates "I can't handle this" into "this is too heavy," shifting the blame off the person and back onto the situation. Good for a friend who's crying from overwork and still apologizing for it.
variations: You're not too weak for the weight. The weight was never meant for one person.
Hitting your limit is a message, not a verdict.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the idea that solitude is life's default and that's what makes companionship precious; rewritten

zh-tw.content:
一個人本來就是人生的預設值，
所以那些願意坐下來陪你的人，
每一個都很值得你記得。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給覺得自己人緣差、朋友太少的人。不是要他去交更多朋友，而是換個角度看：有人願意留下來就已經很不容易了。適合在深夜聊天、對方講到自己很孤單的時候。
variations: 朋友不用多，願意坐下來聽你講完的那幾個就夠了。
陪伴之所以珍貴，是因為它本來就不是理所當然的。

en.content:
Being on your own is life's default setting.
Which is exactly why the people who sit down beside you
are each worth remembering.
en.editorNote: For someone who thinks they're bad at friendship or don't have enough friends. Instead of pushing them to socialize more, it reframes the math: anyone who stays is already rare. Good for a late-night conversation where someone admits they feel alone.
variations: You don't need many friends — just the few who'll sit and hear you out.
Company feels precious because it was never guaranteed in the first place.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the line about warming others in fair weather and warming yourself in cold wind; rewritten

zh-tw.content:
你可以是那種天氣好的時候溫暖別人的人，
但風真的很冷的那幾天，
請先把那份溫暖留給自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種永遠在照顧別人、輪到自己就省略的人。不否定他的善良，只是把順序調回來。適合傳給總是幫人擦眼淚、卻沒人問他好不好的朋友。
variations: 你分給別人的溫柔，記得留一份給自己。
很冷的日子，先顧好自己不是自私，是必要。

en.content:
Be the person who warms others when the weather's kind.
But on the days the wind really cuts,
keep that warmth for yourself first.
en.editorNote: For the person who takes care of everyone and skips their own turn. It doesn't argue with their kindness, just fixes the order. Send to the friend who's always drying someone else's tears while nobody asks how they're doing.
variations: Save a share of the gentleness you hand out to everyone else.
On the coldest days, looking after yourself first isn't selfish. It's necessary.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'someone will warm you with gentleness they've saved up for a long time'; original rewrite on not writing yourself off

zh-tw.content:
先別急著否定自己。
這世界上有人正在攢一份溫柔，
只是還沒走到你面前。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給剛被拒絕、剛失戀，或覺得自己不值得被喜歡的人。重點是「還沒」而不是「沒有」，把否定句改成時間問題。適合在對方說「應該沒有人會喜歡我」的時候回。
variations: 現在沒有人懂你，不等於以後也不會有。
有些溫柔還在路上，別在它到之前就先放棄自己。

en.content:
Don't be so quick to write yourself off.
Somewhere out there someone is saving up a whole lot of gentleness —
they just haven't reached you yet.
en.editorNote: For someone freshly rejected, newly single, or convinced they're unlovable. The key word is "yet" — it turns a verdict into a matter of timing. A good reply when someone says "nobody's ever going to like me."
variations: Nobody gets you right now. That doesn't mean nobody ever will.
Some kindness is still on its way. Don't give up on yourself before it arrives.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Whitney Goodman's Toxic Positivity ('not every situation has a silver lining'); original rewrite pushing back on forced positivity

zh-tw.content:
不用逼自己在每片烏雲裡都找到那條銀邊。
有些事就是很爛，你可以直接說它很爛，
這不叫負面，這叫誠實。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些一難過就馬上被人叫「要往好處想」的人。強行找意義有時比難過本身更累。適合傳給正在硬撐正能量的朋友，讓他知道不用一直演。
variations: 不是每件事都有好的一面，硬要找反而更折磨自己。
承認「這件事真的很糟」，就已經是往前一步了。

en.content:
You don't have to find the silver lining in every cloud.
Some things are just bad, and you're allowed to call them bad.
That's not being negative — that's being honest.
en.editorNote: For anyone who gets told to "look on the bright side" the moment they're upset. Forcing meaning out of pain is sometimes more exhausting than the pain itself. Send to a friend who's performing positivity — let them off the hook.
variations: Not everything has an upside, and hunting for one just wears you out.
Admitting 'this really sucks' is already a step forward.

items.sourceNote: Original writing using a wound-tending metaphor: healing needs air, not constant re-checking

zh-tw.content:
傷口好起來需要的是空氣，
不是你三不五時就掀開來，
檢查它到底好了沒。
別再一直戳它了，讓它靜靜地長。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一直反覆回想同一件事、忍不住去確認「我到底走出來了沒」的人。越檢查越好不了，因為你等於每天重新弄痛它一次。適合失戀或失去後一直反芻的朋友。
variations: 老是回頭確認傷口，它就沒機會結痂。
不用一直問自己好了沒，該好的時候你會知道。

en.content:
A wound heals with a little air —
not with you lifting the bandage every few hours
to check whether it's closed yet.
Stop poking it. Let it knit itself back quietly.
en.editorNote: For the person who keeps replaying the same event, compulsively checking "am I over it yet?" The more you check, the slower it heals — you're reopening it daily. Good for a friend stuck ruminating after a loss or breakup.
variations: Keep peeling back the scab and it never gets to close.
You don't have to keep asking if you're healed. You'll know when you are.

items.sourceNote: Original rewrite pushing back on the pressure to extract a lesson from every hardship ('everything happens for a reason')

zh-tw.content:
你不用把每一次受傷，
都變成一堂課、一段成長、一個更好的自己。
有些痛就只是痛，
你活下來了，這樣就夠了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給被「這都是為了讓你變更好」這種話煩到的人。不是每段苦難都要交出一份收穫報告。有時候撐過去本身就是全部的意義了。適合安慰正在被逼著「感恩」的朋友。
variations: 不是每件壞事背後都藏著禮物，沒有意義也沒關係。
你不欠這段痛苦一個「我學到了什麼」。

en.content:
You don't have to turn every wound
into a lesson, a growth arc, a better version of you.
Sometimes pain is just pain —
and you survived it. That's enough.
en.editorNote: For anyone worn out by "this is all making you stronger." Not every hardship owes you a takeaway report. Sometimes getting through it is the whole point. Good for a friend being pressured to feel grateful.
variations: Not every bad thing is hiding a gift, and meaningless is okay too.
You don't owe this pain a 'here's what I learned.'

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Whitney Goodman on there being no 'appropriate time frame for getting over something'; original rewrite on imposed deadlines

zh-tw.content:
是誰規定你「早該好了」的？
沒有人在你的傷上貼保存期限。
你需要多久，就用多久，
這不是你拖，是你在好好復原。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些被「都過這麼久了還沒走出來」壓著的人。難過沒有標準工時，別人覺得你該好了，不代表你真的好了。適合傳給覺得自己「復原得太慢、很丟臉」的朋友。
variations: 沒有人有資格幫你的悲傷設倒數計時。
你花的時間比別人久，不代表你有問題。

en.content:
Who decided you "should be over it by now"?
Nobody stamped an expiration date on your grief.
Take as long as you need —
that's not you dragging it out, that's you actually healing.
en.editorNote: For anyone crushed by "it's been so long, why aren't you over it?" Sadness doesn't run on a standard schedule, and someone else thinking you should be done doesn't make it true. Send to a friend who feels ashamed of "healing too slowly."
variations: Nobody gets to set a countdown timer on your grief.
Taking longer than other people doesn't mean something's wrong with you.

items.sourceNote: Original writing using a broken-bone / cast metaphor to reframe 'not wanting to do anything' as necessary immobilization

zh-tw.content:
骨頭斷了要打石膏、固定不動，才長得回去。
你現在的「什麼都不想做」，
可能就是你的心在幫自己打石膏。
它不是壞掉了，是在等接回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一放空就覺得自己在爛、在浪費生命的人。把「動不了」重新定義成「正在固定復原」，罪惡感會少很多。適合傳給責怪自己太廢的朋友。
variations: 動不了不是懶，是你需要先固定住才長得回來。
石膏拆掉之前不能亂動，你的心也一樣，急不得。

en.content:
A broken bone has to be set in a cast and kept still to grow back.
That "I don't want to do anything" you're feeling right now
might just be your heart putting itself in a cast.
It's not broken — it's waiting to knit back together.
en.editorNote: For the person who feels like they're rotting or wasting their life the moment they slow down. Reframing "can't move" as "being held still to heal" takes a lot of the guilt out. Send to a friend beating themselves up for being unproductive.
variations: Not moving isn't laziness — you have to be set in place before you can mend.
You can't rush a cast off early, and you can't rush your heart either.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the 'always the strong one' dynamic; reframes being caught, not just catching others

zh-tw.content:
你一直是那個接住所有人的人，
那誰來接住你？
你也可以偶爾把手鬆開，
讓別人扶你一下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種在群組裡永遠回「我沒事」、大家難過都來找他、自己崩潰時卻不知道能找誰的人。適合傳給那個總是很可靠、很少喊累的朋友。
variations: 當那個很強的人也會累，你也有資格偶爾當那個被照顧的人。
你不用一直堅強給大家看，鬆一口氣也沒關係。

en.content:
You're always the one catching everyone else —
so who catches you?
You're allowed to let go sometimes
and let someone hold you up too.
en.editorNote: For the person who's always 'fine' in the group chat, the one everyone leans on, but who has no idea who to call when they fall apart. Send to the friend who's endlessly dependable and never admits they're tired.
variations: Being the strong one is exhausting — you're allowed to be the one who gets taken care of sometimes.
You don't have to keep performing strength for everyone. It's okay to let your guard down.

items.sourceNote: Original writing reframing asking for help as an act of trust rather than a burden

zh-tw.content:
開口求助不是給人添麻煩，
是你願意相信這段關係
撐得住你真實的樣子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種寧可自己硬扛，也不敢麻煩別人的人。把「求助」重新看成一種信任，而不是負擔。適合傳給那個什麼都自己來、從不喊救命的朋友。
variations: 需要幫忙的時候說一聲，不會讓你變得比較弱，只會讓在乎你的人有機會靠近。
會願意讓你麻煩的人，其實根本不覺得那是麻煩。

en.content:
Asking for help isn't being a burden —
it's trusting that this relationship
can hold the real, unpolished you.
en.editorNote: For the person who'd rather quietly struggle than bother anyone. Reframes reaching out as an act of trust, not a liability. Send to the friend who does everything alone and never says 'help.'
variations: Saying you need help doesn't make you weaker — it just lets the people who care get close enough to reach you.
The people who let you lean on them don't actually think of it as a bother.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on permission to feel joy mid-grief; sadness and happiness can coexist

zh-tw.content:
就算日子很難，
你還是可以笑一下。
那一秒的開心不是背叛你的難過，
只是你的心在偷偷喘口氣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一笑出來就有罪惡感、覺得自己「沒資格開心」的人。難過跟快樂可以同時存在，笑一下不代表你不痛了。適合傳給正在低潮、卻因為短暫快樂而自責的朋友。
variations: 在最糟的時候還能笑，不是麻木，是你身上還有活著的力氣。
你可以一邊還很痛，一邊允許自己享受一點點好事。

en.content:
Even when things are hard,
you're still allowed to laugh.
That second of joy isn't a betrayal of your sadness —
it's just your heart sneaking in a breath.
en.editorNote: For the person who feels guilty the moment they smile, like they haven't 'earned' happiness. Grief and joy can coexist; laughing doesn't mean you've stopped hurting. Send to a friend in a low place beating themselves up over a brief moment of lightness.
variations: Being able to laugh at the worst of it isn't numbness — it's proof you've still got some life in you.
You can still be hurting and let yourself enjoy a small good thing at the same time.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Jamie Anderson's 'grief is just love with nowhere to go'; rewritten as gentle permission

zh-tw.content:
你以為那是放不下，
其實那是一份還沒送出去的愛。
它沒有錯，只是暫時找不到能給的地方了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給還在想念某個人、卻覺得自己「怎麼還沒好」的人。想念不是你不夠堅強，是你心裡的愛還在，只是收件人不在了。適合傳給正在思念遠方或離開的人的朋友。
variations: 還會想他，不代表你退步了，只代表你曾經很認真地愛過。
那份愛沒有消失，它只是還在等一個新的方向。

en.content:
What you call not being able to let go
is really just love that has nowhere to land.
There's nothing wrong with it —
it just lost its address for a while.
en.editorNote: For the person still missing someone and wondering why they 'aren't over it yet.' Missing them isn't weakness; it's love that's still here, just without a recipient. Send to a friend grieving someone far away or gone.
variations: Still thinking about them isn't backsliding — it means you loved for real.
That love didn't disappear. It's just waiting for a new direction to point in.

items.sourceNote: Original angle: grieving a future/version of life that won't happen, not just a past loss

zh-tw.content:
有時候你難過的，
不是失去了什麼，
而是那個你以為會發生、後來卻沒發生的未來。
那個未來也值得被好好道別。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些說不清自己在難過什麼的人——常常不是失去了現在的東西，而是失去了想像中的某個版本。承認你在替一個沒發生的未來哀悼，本身就是一種放過自己。
variations: 你可以想念一個從來沒真正到來過的日子。
跟腦海裡那個「本來可以」好好說再見，也是一種前進。

en.content:
Sometimes the ache isn't about
what you lost —
it's about the future you were so sure would come, and didn't.
That future deserves a proper goodbye too.
en.editorNote: For anyone who can't name what they're grieving. Often it's not a present loss but an imagined version of life that never arrived. Letting yourself mourn a future that won't happen is its own kind of release.
variations: You're allowed to miss a day that never actually came.
Saying goodbye to the 'it could have been' in your head is also a way forward.

items.sourceNote: Original: ambivalence — missing someone and being relieved they're gone can coexist

zh-tw.content:
你可以一邊想念一個人，
一邊慶幸他已經不在你的生活裡了。
這兩種感覺同時存在，
不代表你矛盾，只代表你很誠實。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些結束一段關係後、又想念又鬆一口氣、覺得自己「是不是有問題」的人。複雜的感覺不是錯亂，是人本來就會這樣。適合傳給剛離開一段耗損關係的朋友。
variations: 想念他，跟不想回去，可以同時是真的。
你不用逼自己只能有一種感覺，心本來就裝得下相反的東西。

en.content:
You can miss someone
and be relieved they're no longer in your life,
at the same time.
Holding both doesn't make you contradictory —
it makes you honest.
en.editorNote: For anyone who ended a relationship and feels both longing and relief, then wonders if something's wrong with them. Mixed feelings aren't confusion; hearts just hold opposites. Send to a friend who just walked away from something draining.
variations: Missing them and not wanting to go back can both be true.
You don't have to pick one feeling — a heart has room for opposite things.

items.sourceNote: Original angle: nostalgia is missing a version of yourself, not the time/place itself

zh-tw.content:
你懷念的可能不是那段時光，
而是那時候的自己——
還沒受過那些傷、還敢隨便相信的那個人。
他沒有不見，他只是變得比較小心了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些常說「好想回到以前」的人。懷念的其實不是某個地方或某一年，是那個更輕鬆、更敢的自己。他還在你身上，只是學會了保護自己而已。
variations: 你想回去的不是那一年，是那一年裡還沒學會設防的你。
以前那個你沒有死掉，他只是長出了一層殼。

en.content:
Maybe you don't miss that time —
you miss who you were in it:
the version of you that hadn't been hurt yet, that still trusted easily.
He didn't vanish. He just got more careful.
en.editorNote: For anyone who keeps saying 'I wish I could go back.' What you miss usually isn't a place or a year — it's the lighter, braver version of yourself. He's still in there; he just learned to protect himself.
variations: You don't want that year back — you want the you who hadn't learned to guard yet.
The old you didn't die. He just grew a shell.

items.sourceNote: 2026 trend: 'quiet burnout' — people masking exhaustion while still functioning; rewritten as gentle permission

zh-tw.content:
你沒有崩潰，事情也都準時做完了，
所以沒有人發現，
連你自己都被騙過去。
但「還能運轉」跟「還好」，從來不是同一件事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些外表一切正常、內在早就空了的人。很多疲憊不會有明顯的徵兆，只是安靜地把你耗光。你不需要先崩潰一次，才有資格說自己撐不住了。
variations: 你不用等到真的倒下來，才准許自己說一句「我累了」。
把事情做完了，不代表你沒事，只代表你很會忍。

en.content:
You didn't fall apart. Everything got done on time.
So nobody noticed —
including you.
But still functioning and actually okay
have never been the same thing.
en.editorNote: For the person who looks completely fine and is running on empty. Some exhaustion has no obvious symptoms; it just quietly drains you. You don't have to break down first to earn the right to say you're tired.
variations: You don't have to collapse before you're allowed to say 'I'm worn out.'
Getting it all done doesn't mean you're fine. It means you're good at enduring.

items.sourceNote: 2026 trend: self-care itself has become another performance metric; original angle — rest has no correct method

zh-tw.content:
現在連休息都有正確做法了：
要早睡、要伸展、要記得感恩三件事。
沒做到就覺得自己連放鬆都失敗。
可是休息沒有及格線，
它只要讓你舒服，就已經做對了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些把自我照顧變成另一張待辦清單、然後被清單追著跑的人。當放鬆變成要打卡的功課，它就不再是休息了。今天躺著發呆一小時，什麼都沒記錄，也完全算數。
variations: 你不用休得很好看，你只要休得夠。
如果照顧自己讓你更焦慮，那你照顧的可能不是自己，是別人的標準。

en.content:
Even rest has a correct method now:
sleep early, stretch, log three things you're grateful for.
Miss one and you feel like you failed at relaxing.
But rest has no passing grade.
If it made you feel better, you already did it right.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose self-care turned into another to-do list that's now chasing them. The moment relaxing becomes something you have to log, it stops being rest. An hour of lying there doing nothing, untracked, absolutely counts.
variations: You don't have to rest impressively. You just have to rest enough.
If taking care of yourself makes you more anxious, you might be taking care of someone else's standards.

items.sourceNote: Summer 2026 burnout-recovery travel trend; original angle — it takes days before a tense body believes it can stop

zh-tw.content:
放假第一天你還在想工作，
第二天睡到頭痛，
第三天才終於有一點點鬆下來的感覺。
不是你不會放鬆，
是你繃太久了，
身體需要一點時間，才敢相信這次真的可以停。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些覺得「休假好像也沒有比較好」而自責的人。長期緊繃的人放鬆是有延遲的，前幾天的空虛和頭痛都是正常的。給自己比想像中更長的緩衝，別一放假就急著檢查自己有沒有變好。
variations: 鬆下來是有時差的，別怪自己第一天還沒感覺。
你不是不會休息，你只是已經很久沒有被允許停下來了。

en.content:
Day one off, you're still thinking about work.
Day two, you sleep until your head hurts.
Day three, something in you finally loosens.
You're not bad at relaxing —
you've just been braced for so long
that your body needs time to believe it's really allowed to stop.
en.editorNote: For anyone who feels guilty that time off didn't 'work.' When you've been tense for months, relief runs on a delay — the empty, headachy first days are normal. Give yourself a longer runway, and stop checking whether you've improved yet.
variations: Letting go has a lag. Don't blame yourself for not feeling it on day one.
You're not bad at resting. You just haven't been allowed to stop in a very long time.

items.sourceNote: Original metaphor: low power mode as a valid state of operating, not being broken

zh-tw.content:
你只是進入低耗電模式而已。
螢幕調暗一點、背景的東西先關掉、
動作慢一點、回訊息慢一點。
那不是壞掉，
那是還在運作的另一種樣子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些覺得自己「最近整個人很鈍」的人。反應變慢、社交變少、只做最必要的事，不是退化，是身體幫你省電。等電量回來，那些功能自己會再打開。
variations: 只做最低限度的事，也是一種撐下去的方式。
你沒有故障，你只是把不必要的功能先關掉了。

en.content:
You're just in low power mode.
Screen dimmed, background stuff shut off,
moving slower, replying slower.
That isn't broken.
That's another way of still running.
en.editorNote: For anyone who feels dulled lately. Slower reactions, less socializing, doing only the essentials — that's not decline, that's your system conserving. When the charge comes back, those features turn themselves on again.
variations: Doing only the bare minimum is also a way of getting through.
Nothing's malfunctioning. You just turned off the features you couldn't afford right now.

items.sourceNote: Original framing on holding two truths at once: gratitude and exhaustion can coexist without contradiction

zh-tw.content:
你可以很愛你的生活，同時也累得想暫停一下。
這兩件事不衝突，也都是真的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些覺得「我明明過得不差，怎麼還這麼累」而自責的人。日子好好的和你很疲憊可以同時存在，不需要因為擁有一些幸福，就覺得自己沒資格喊累。
variations: 感恩和疲憊可以住在同一天裡，你沒有不知足。
不是你不懂珍惜，只是再喜歡的生活也需要休息。

en.content:
You can love your life and still be tired enough to want to pause.
Those two things don't cancel out — they're both true.
en.editorNote: For anyone who feels guilty thinking 'my life isn't even bad, why am I this drained?' A good life and deep exhaustion can share the same day. Having some happiness doesn't disqualify you from being tired.
variations: Gratitude and exhaustion can live in the same day. You're not ungrateful.
It's not that you don't appreciate it — even a life you love still needs rest.

items.sourceNote: Original angle distinguishing forgiveness from reconciliation; permission to forgive without re-admitting someone

zh-tw.content:
你可以原諒一個人，同時不再讓他回到你的生活。
原諒是為了把事情放下，不是為了把門重新打開。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些被勸「都過去了就和好吧」而覺得為難的人。原諒和放行是兩回事——你可以在心裡把結解開，同時繼續把某些人留在門外。放下不欠誰一個回頭。
variations: 和解是給自己的，不一定要分對方一份。
你把怨恨放下了，不代表你欠對方一個重來的機會。

en.content:
You can forgive someone and still not let them back in.
Forgiveness is for putting it down — not for reopening the door.
en.editorNote: For anyone pressured with 'it's in the past, just make up.' Forgiving and allowing back are two different things. You can untie the knot inside you and still keep certain people on the other side of the door. Letting go doesn't owe anyone a way back.
variations: Making peace is for you. You don't have to hand a copy to them.
Putting down the resentment doesn't mean you owe them another chance.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on permission to change one's mind as self-honesty rather than flakiness

zh-tw.content:
你可以改變主意。
昨天說好的事，今天覺得不對，就可以喊停。
那不是善變，是你比昨天更了解自己了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些一旦答應就硬著頭皮做完、怕被說「怎麼又反悔」的人。人是會變的，多知道一點、多累一點，答案就可能不一樣。改變主意不是不負責任，是對現在的自己誠實。
variations: 反悔不是背叛承諾，是你長出了新的判斷。
你有權利在更懂自己之後，做出不一樣的選擇。

en.content:
You're allowed to change your mind.
What you agreed to yesterday can stop today if it no longer feels right.
That's not being flaky — it's knowing yourself better than you did yesterday.
en.editorNote: For anyone who forces themselves to finish whatever they agreed to, afraid of hearing 'why'd you back out?' People change; a little more knowledge, a little more fatigue, and the answer can shift. Changing your mind isn't irresponsible — it's being honest about who you are now.
variations: Backing out isn't betraying a promise. It's a new judgment you grew into.
You have the right to choose differently once you understand yourself better.

items.sourceNote: Original framing on choosing peace over being right; conserving energy by not engaging every conflict

zh-tw.content:
不是每一場爭吵都需要你贏。
有些對話，你選擇不回應，
不是因為你輸了，
是因為你的平靜比證明自己對更重要。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些明明很累還忍不住想把道理講清楚的人。不是每句話都值得你花力氣去接。把「我一定要讓他懂」放下，有時候是留給自己最後一點電量。安靜離開一場沒有結果的爭執，也是一種贏。
variations: 你不用參加每一場別人邀請你吵的架。
有些事你選擇不爭，不是退讓，是你更想要安穩。

en.content:
Not every argument needs you to win it.
Some conversations you choose not to answer —
not because you lost,
but because your peace matters more than being proven right.
en.editorNote: For anyone who's exhausted but still can't resist setting the record straight. Not every remark deserves your energy. Putting down 'I have to make them understand' can be how you save your last bit of charge. Walking quietly away from a pointless fight is its own kind of winning.
variations: You don't have to attend every argument you're invited to.
Choosing not to fight for something isn't backing down — it's wanting calm more.

items.sourceNote: Original framing on self-compassion; the gap between how we treat others and how we treat ourselves

zh-tw.content:
你對每個朋友都那麼溫柔，
只有對自己，開口就是嫌棄。
試著把你會對朋友說的那句話，
也留一句給自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種安慰別人一流、罵自己也一流的人。你不會對搞砸的朋友說「你怎麼這麼廢」，那為什麼捨得這樣對自己。適合傳給總是把自己排在最後一個的朋友。
variations: 你借別人的那份體諒，記得也留一點給自己。
如果朋友這樣累，你會叫他休息；那你呢？

en.content:
You're so gentle with everyone else,
and the second it's you, it's all criticism.
Try saying to yourself
what you'd say to a friend.
en.editorNote: For the person who's world-class at comforting others and world-class at trashing themselves. You'd never tell a friend who messed up 'you're such a screwup' — so why is it fine to say it to you? Send to the friend who always puts themselves last.
variations: Save a little of the patience you lend everyone else — for you.
If a friend were this tired, you'd tell them to rest. So what about you?

items.sourceNote: Original framing pushing back on self-improvement pressure; worth is not conditional on becoming 'better'

zh-tw.content:
你不用先變成更好的版本，
才配得上休息、配得上被愛。
現在這個還沒變好的你，
就已經可以了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種永遠覺得「等我再厲害一點就好」的人。你把善待自己設成了達標獎勵，可是你根本不用先過關。適合傳給總在追下一個目標、忘記自己現在也很好的朋友。
variations: 不用等到瘦下來、升職、變厲害，你現在就值得對自己好。
你不是變好才有價值，你本來就有。

en.content:
You don't have to become a better version
to deserve rest, or to deserve love.
The you that hasn't gotten there yet
is already allowed.
en.editorNote: For the person always thinking 'once I'm a little more impressive, then.' You've turned being kind to yourself into a reward for hitting a target — but there's no target to clear first. Send to the friend forever chasing the next goal, forgetting they're already enough.
variations: You don't have to wait to be thinner, promoted, or sharper — you're worth kindness now.
You're not valuable once you improve. You already were.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the pressure to make every day meaningful; permission for an ordinary day

zh-tw.content:
今天沒有進步、沒有收穫、
什麼特別的事都沒發生，
就只是普普通通過完了，
這樣也很好，不用交代。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一到晚上就檢討「今天到底做了什麼」的人。不是每天都得有成長、有意義、有產值。平平安安過完一天，本身就夠了。適合傳給把每天都當成績單在打分數的自己。
variations: 不是每一天都要有意義，有些日子的任務就是好好過完。
今天平淡不是浪費，是你難得的喘息。

en.content:
No progress today, nothing gained,
nothing special happened —
just an ordinary day, lived through.
That's fine too. No need to justify it.
en.editorNote: For the person who hits every night with 'so what did I actually do today?' Not every day has to grow you, mean something, or produce output. Getting safely through a day is enough on its own. Send to the you who grades each day like a report card.
variations: Not every day needs meaning — some days the whole task is just getting through them.
A plain day isn't wasted. It's the breather you rarely let yourself have.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on recovery not needing an audience or proof; permission to heal privately

zh-tw.content:
你的好起來，不需要證明給任何人看。
沒有人在計分，也沒有觀眾在等你表演康復。
你自己知道有沒有好一點，這樣就夠了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種連難過都好像要做給別人看、連振作都怕不夠有說服力的人。復原不是一場表演，沒有評審，也沒有及格線。適合傳給那個總覺得要向誰交代自己過得好不好的人。
variations: 你不用把傷口拿給每個人看，也不用證明它已經好了。
好起來是你自己的事，不必開放參觀。

en.content:
Your healing doesn't have to be proven to anyone.
No one's keeping score, and there's no audience waiting for you to perform recovery.
You know if you're a little better. That's enough.
en.editorNote: For the person who feels like even their sadness has to look convincing, and their bouncing back has to be persuasive enough. Recovery isn't a performance — no judges, no passing grade. Send to the friend who always feels they owe someone proof that they're okay.
variations: You don't have to show your wound to everyone, or prove it's already closed.
Getting better is your own business. It's not open for viewing.

items.sourceNote: Original writing using the moon-phase metaphor for accepting off-days; nature-based gentle framing

zh-tw.content:
月亮不會因為今天缺了一角，就覺得自己壞了。
它只是換了一個樣子，繼續掛在天上。
你也可以，不用每天都圓滿發光。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給覺得自己「狀態不好就是不對」的人。月亮從缺到圓本來就是循環，沒有哪一天的月亮是失敗的。你今天暗一點、缺一角，也還是完整地在那裡。適合貼在心情低落的夜晚。
variations: 有時候你只是走到月缺的那幾天，不是不見了，只是暫時收起光。
不用每天都是滿月，缺的時候也還是月亮。

en.content:
The moon doesn't think it's broken just because tonight it's missing a piece.
It simply wears a different shape and stays up in the sky.
You're allowed to do the same — you don't have to be full and glowing every day.
en.editorNote: For anyone who believes 'a bad state means something's wrong with me.' Waxing and waning is just the moon's cycle — no single night's moon is a failure. Even dimmer, even a sliver, you're still fully there. Keep this for the low nights.
variations: Some nights you're just in your waning days — not gone, only holding your light for a while.
You don't have to be a full moon every night. Even a crescent is still the moon.

items.sourceNote: Original writing using a save-point / log-off game metaphor for permission to rest before finishing

zh-tw.content:
今天先存檔吧。
不用一次把整個關卡打完，
明天回來，從這裡繼續就好。
下線休息，也是遊戲的一部分。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種覺得「沒做完就不能休息」的人。人生不是一口氣通關的遊戲，累了就存個檔、先下線，進度不會消失。適合傳給熬夜硬撐、捨不得停下來的自己。
variations: 進度存好了，不會不見，你可以安心先去睡。
今天打到這裡就好，明天再繼續，不用一次全破。

en.content:
Save your progress for today.
You don't have to clear the whole level in one sitting —
come back tomorrow and pick up right here.
Logging off to rest is part of the game too.
en.editorNote: For the person who feels they can't rest until it's all done. Life isn't a game you have to beat in one run — when you're tired, save and log off; your progress won't vanish. Send to the you who keeps pushing through the night, unwilling to stop.
variations: Your progress is saved. It won't disappear — you can go to sleep in peace.
Stop here for today. Continue tomorrow. You don't have to finish it all at once.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the chapter-comparison trap of social media; reframing a slow start as not falling behind

zh-tw.content:
別拿你的第一章，去比別人的第二十章。
他們走過的那些你沒看到的路，
你才剛要開始走而已。
慢，不代表你落後。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一打開社群軟體就覺得自己輸很多的人。你看到的是別人的中段甚至結局，卻拿來對比自己的開頭。起步的慢，從來不是失敗。適合傳給老是覺得「別人都比我快」的自己。
variations: 你看到的是別人的精華片段，不是他熬過的每一集。
剛起步的你，本來就不該跟走到一半的人比進度。

en.content:
Don't measure your chapter one against someone's chapter twenty.
All the roads they walked that you never saw —
you're only just starting yours.
Slow doesn't mean you're behind.
en.editorNote: For the person who opens social media and instantly feels like they're losing. What you see is someone's middle, maybe their ending — and you're holding it up against your beginning. Starting slow was never failure. Send to the you who keeps thinking 'everyone's faster than me.'
variations: What you're seeing is someone's highlight reel, not every episode they lived through.
Just getting started, you were never meant to match the pace of someone halfway through.

items.sourceNote: Original writing riffing on the 2026 self-compassion theme of asking what you need from the day instead of what the day needs from you

zh-tw.content:
早上醒來，先別急著問「今天有什麼事要做」。
換一個問法：「今天的我，需要什麼？」
可能是多睡十分鐘、
可能是一頓不趕時間的早餐、
可能是今天什麼都不答應。
先聽自己一次，再去聽行事曆。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合睜眼就開始盤點待辦事項的人。把「今天要我做什麼」和「我今天需要什麼」換個順序，一天的手感會差很多。可以設成手機桌布或早上第一則提醒。
variations: 行事曆會一直跟你要東西，記得也留一格問問自己想要什麼。
在被今天推著走之前，先問自己一句：我現在需要的是什麼？

en.content:
When you wake up, don't start with "what has to get done today."
Try the other question: "what do I need today?"
Maybe ten more minutes of sleep.
Maybe breakfast you don't have to rush.
Maybe saying yes to nothing at all.
Check in with yourself first, then check the calendar.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose eyes open straight into a to-do list. Flipping the order of 'what the day wants from me' and 'what I need today' changes the whole texture of the hours that follow. Works well as a lock screen or the first reminder of the morning.
variations: Your calendar will keep asking things of you. Leave one slot to ask yourself something.
Before the day starts pushing you around, ask what you actually need from it.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on low-capacity days and the shame attached to undone household tasks

zh-tw.content:
水槽裡還沒洗的碗、
沙發上那堆沒摺的衣服，
它們不是你的人格評分表。
那只代表你今天的電量剛好用在別的地方了。
碗明天洗還是會乾淨的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種累到什麼都做不動、卻又因為家裡很亂而更討厭自己的日子。家事沒做完不等於做人失敗。適合傳給正躺在一片混亂裡自責的朋友。
variations: 沒摺的衣服不會定義你，它只是還沒被摺而已。
家裡亂不代表你這個人亂，只代表你今天的力氣先用在撐過去了。

en.content:
The dishes still in the sink,
the laundry pile that never made it off the couch —
those aren't a scorecard on who you are.
They just mean today's energy went somewhere else.
The dishes will still wash clean tomorrow.
en.editorNote: For the days when you're too drained to do anything, and then hate yourself extra because the place is a mess. An undone chore is not a failed character. Send it to the friend currently lying in the middle of the chaos, feeling bad about it.
variations: Unfolded laundry doesn't define you. It's just laundry that hasn't been folded.
A messy home doesn't mean a messy person. It means your energy went into getting through today.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on summer-heat fatigue and mistaking weather-driven slowness for laziness

zh-tw.content:
這種天氣，光是出門走到路口就滿身汗，
回到家只想癱著什麼都不想。
那不是你變懶了，
是你的身體正在很努力地幫你降溫。
夏天的你，效率本來就可以低一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 七、八月專用。天氣熱到什麼都做不動的時候，人很容易誤會成自己意志力不夠。其實光是在高溫裡活著就已經在消耗你了。適合在午後最熱的那個時段傳給同樣被曬扁的朋友。
variations: 熱到腦袋轉不動不是你的錯，是氣溫先出手的。
夏天做得比較少很正常，你有一半的力氣都拿去對抗熱了。

en.content:
In this heat, walking to the corner leaves you soaked,
and the second you're home you just want to melt into the couch.
That isn't you getting lazy.
That's your body working overtime to keep you cool.
Summer you is allowed to run at a lower speed.
en.editorNote: Built for July and August. When it's too hot to do anything, it's easy to mistake the slowness for weak willpower — but simply existing in that heat is already spending you. Good to send during the worst hour of the afternoon to a friend who's equally flattened.
variations: If your brain won't turn over in this heat, that's the temperature's doing, not yours.
Getting less done in summer is normal. Half your energy is already going to not overheating.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on reply-speed guilt and reframing slow responses as capacity, not indifference

zh-tw.content:
沒有秒回，不代表你不在乎。
有時候你只是還沒有力氣，
把一句像樣的話組起來。
真的在乎你的人，
等得起你慢慢回的那幾個小時。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種看到訊息心裡一緊、又回不出來，然後開始愧疚的人。回訊息的速度從來不是感情的溫度計。適合傳給總覺得自己「已讀很久很沒禮貌」的朋友。
variations: 訊息晚幾個小時回，不會把一段關係弄壞。
你不是冷淡，你只是把僅剩的力氣先留給自己了。

en.content:
Not replying right away doesn't mean you don't care.
Sometimes you just don't have the energy yet
to put a decent sentence together.
The people who actually care about you
can wait the few hours it takes.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose chest tightens at an unread message, who can't answer, and then spirals into guilt about it. Reply speed was never a thermometer for how much you love someone. Send it to the friend who keeps apologizing for leaving people on read.
variations: A message answered a few hours late has never broken a real relationship.
You're not being cold. You're just spending the last of your energy on yourself first.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on enjoying a hobby badly, without turning it into output or a side hustle

zh-tw.content:
你可以喜歡一件事，然後做得很爛。
不用練到能拿出來給人看，
不用想著哪天能不能接案、能不能變成副業。
有些事的意義就是：
你在做的時候，心裡是鬆的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一開始新的興趣，就忍不住想「這能不能變現」的人。不是每件喜歡的事都得長成作品或收入。適合傳給連放鬆都要有產出的自己。
variations: 畫得很醜也可以繼續畫，那是你的，不是要交出去的。
有些喜歡的事不用進步，它的用途就是讓你喘一口氣。

en.content:
You're allowed to love something and be bad at it.
You don't have to get good enough to show anyone.
You don't have to wonder whether it could take clients someday, or become a side hustle.
Some things exist for one reason:
while you're doing them, something in you loosens.
en.editorNote: For the person who picks up a new hobby and immediately asks whether it could make money. Not everything you enjoy has to grow into a portfolio or an income stream. Send it to the version of you that needs even relaxing to produce something.
variations: Draw it badly and keep going. It's yours, not something you owe anyone.
Some things you love don't need to improve. Their whole job is letting you breathe.

items.sourceNote: Mindful.org 談自我疼惜與飲食自責的循環；改寫成冰箱裡沒煮的食材場景

zh-tw.content:
冰箱最下層那包已經爛掉的青菜，
你不用為它罵自己。
買它的那天，你是真心想好好照顧自己的。
只是那個星期，力氣剛好不夠煮它。
那份心意沒有壞掉，它還在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「明明想好好生活卻做不到」而自責的時刻。也可以傳給買了一堆健康食材、結果整週都吃外送的朋友。
variations: 買菜的那個你，跟沒力氣煮的這個你，是同一個人。他們都在盡力。
菜可以丟，但那份想照顧自己的心留下來就好。

en.content:
That bag of greens going soft at the back of your fridge—
you don't owe yourself a lecture over it.
The day you bought it, you honestly meant to take care of yourself.
That week just didn't leave you the energy to cook it.
The intention didn't spoil. That part's still good.
en.editorNote: For the moment you're beating yourself up because you meant to live better and didn't. Also good for the friend who buys a fridge full of vegetables and orders delivery all week.
variations: The you who bought the groceries and the you too tired to cook them are the same person. Both were doing their best.
Throw out the vegetables. Keep the part of you that wanted to feed you well.

items.sourceNote: Kristin Neff 對自我疼惜的定義（善待自己而非嚴厲評判）；改寫成收藏夾裡沒看完的文章場景

zh-tw.content:
你的收藏夾裡存了三十幾篇「怎麼好好愛自己」，
一篇都沒看完。
那不是你不上進。
按下收藏的那一秒，
你已經替自己說過一句：我想被好好對待。
那句話，比那三十篇加起來都重要。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合存滿了心理成長內容、卻一直沒力氣打開的人。也可以貼在自己的備忘錄裡，提醒自己不必先做完功課才配好過。
variations: 你不是懶得看，是你現在需要的不是方法，是有人告訴你：你已經可以了。
那些沒看完的收藏，是你還想好起來的證據。

en.content:
You've saved thirty-something articles about being kinder to yourself.
Haven't finished a single one.
That's not you slacking off.
The second you hit save, you'd already said it out loud:
I want to be treated well.
That sentence matters more than all thirty of them put together.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose saved folder is stuffed with self-growth reading they never have the energy to open. Works as a note to yourself, too: you don't have to finish the homework before you're allowed to feel okay.
variations: You're not too lazy to read them. You just need someone to say you're already enough, not another method.
Every article you saved and never opened is proof you still want to get better.

items.sourceNote: 自我疼惜指南中「共通人性、不必因羞愧而孤立自己」的概念；改寫成留意陌生人小小善意的場景

zh-tw.content:
今天撐住你的，可能不是什麼大道理。
是店員把熱食遞過來時多說的那句「小心燙」，
是有人幫你按住電梯門，
是路口有人先讓你過。
在你覺得沒人在意的那天，
其實還是有人對你溫柔了一下，
只是他們剛好都不認識你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合覺得自己被世界忘記的那種夜晚。可以傳給孤單的朋友，也可以自己回想一下：今天有誰對你好過一下？
variations: 不是每一份溫柔都會自我介紹。
那些不認識你的人，今天也對你好過一下，只是你當時沒空注意。

en.content:
What got you through today probably wasn't some big insight.
It was the clerk saying "careful, it's hot" as they handed it over.
Someone holding the elevator.
Someone waving you across first.
On the day you felt like nobody cared,
a few people were still gentle with you—
they just happened to be strangers.
en.editorNote: For the kind of night where you feel forgotten by everyone. Send it to a friend who's lonely, or use it yourself to go back through the day and count who was kind to you.
variations: Not every bit of kindness introduces itself.
People who don't even know your name were good to you today. You were just too tired to notice.

items.sourceNote: 2026 心理健康趨勢談神經系統調節（身體停留在警戒狀態、需要時間回到安全）；改寫成「不是玻璃心，是警報還沒關」的安撫語句

zh-tw.content:
一件小事就讓你心跳加速，你以為自己太脆弱。
其實不是。
你的身體只是還停在上次那場風暴裡，
警報還沒收到「已經過去了」的通知。
它不是壞掉，它是保護你保護得太認真了。
給它一點時間，它會慢慢把音量調小。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種明明沒事發生、身體卻先緊繃起來的時刻。也可以傳給總是自責「我怎麼反應這麼大」的朋友，讓他知道那是身體在盡責，不是人格缺陷。
variations: 你的反應不誇張，只是你的身體記性比你好。
警報還在響，不代表危險還在，只代表它還沒被告知你已經安全了。

en.content:
A small thing sends your heart racing and you decide you're fragile.
You're not.
Your body is still standing in the last storm,
waiting for someone to tell the alarm it's over.
It isn't broken. It's just been guarding you a little too faithfully.
Give it time, and it will turn the volume down.
en.editorNote: For the moments when nothing is happening but your body braces anyway. Also good for the friend who keeps apologizing for 'overreacting' — that's a nervous system doing its job, not a character flaw.
variations: Your reaction isn't dramatic. Your body just has a longer memory than you do.
An alarm still ringing doesn't mean danger. It means nobody has told it you're safe yet.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年度趨勢文談「把生活過成專案」的疲勞；改寫成年中回看年初目標清單的場景

zh-tw.content:
一月的時候你寫下一整頁想變成的樣子，
七個月過去，那頁還是空的。
可是這七個月你也沒有白過——
你撐過了幾個很難的星期，
你在誰都沒看見的時候把自己扶起來過。
那些沒被寫進清單的，才是你真正做到的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合月底、年中回頭檢討自己的時刻。年度目標沒完成不代表這段日子沒有意義。可以在七月最後一天傳給正在盤點自己的朋友。
variations: 清單沒打勾，不等於這半年是空的。
有些事沒辦法寫進目標欄，例如你今年撐過了幾次想放棄的念頭。

en.content:
In January you wrote a full page of who you meant to become.
Seven months later the boxes are still empty.
But these seven months weren't wasted —
you got through some genuinely hard weeks,
you picked yourself up when nobody was watching.
The things that never made the list are the ones you actually did.
en.editorNote: For the end of a month, or the middle of a year, when you start auditing yourself. Unfinished goals don't make the time meaningless. Nice to send on the last day of July to a friend taking stock.
variations: An unchecked box doesn't make half a year empty.
Some things don't fit in a goals column — like how many times this year you wanted to quit and didn't.

items.sourceNote: 2026 報導談大腦無法負荷持續壞消息造成的疲勞；改寫成睡前滑新聞後莫名沉重的場景

zh-tw.content:
睡前那半小時，你滑過了戰爭、災難、誰又出事了，
然後躺下來，覺得胸口悶悶的，卻說不出為什麼。
那不是你想太多，
是你一個晚上替整個世界難過了太多次。
關掉螢幕不是冷漠，
是承認你的心也只有一顆，需要休息。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合睡前忍不住一直滑壞消息的人。心情變差常常不是生活出問題，是資訊量超載。可以設成睡前提醒，或傳給那個總說「最近莫名很低落」的朋友。
variations: 你不是心情不好，是今天替太多陌生人心痛過。
你的心可以在乎世界，但它不必二十四小時營業。

en.content:
In the last half hour before bed you scrolled past a war, a disaster, someone else's worst day.
Then you lay down with a weight on your chest and no name for it.
That's not you being oversensitive.
You grieved for the whole world a dozen times in one evening.
Closing the screen isn't indifference.
It's admitting you only have one heart, and it needs to rest.
en.editorNote: For anyone who can't stop scrolling bad news at night. The heaviness usually isn't your life falling apart — it's sheer input overload. Works as a bedtime reminder, or a message to the friend who keeps saying they feel low for no reason.
variations: You're not in a bad mood. You spent today aching for strangers.
Your heart is allowed to care about the world without being open twenty-four hours.

items.sourceNote: 2026 健康趨勢強調「光線、空氣、移動」等低門檻日常調節；改寫成低能量日子裡開窗站三分鐘的場景

zh-tw.content:
如果今天真的什麼都做不到，
那就去把窗戶推開，站三分鐘。
讓風碰一下你的臉，
讓外面的聲音提醒你世界還在運轉。
照顧自己不一定要早起、運動、寫日記，
有時候它就只是——換一口新鮮的空氣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種連起身都很費力的日子。門檻壓到最低的自我照顧提案，做得到就已經很好。適合在下午最沉重的時候傳給自己或朋友。
variations: 做不到大的，就做小的。開窗也算。
今天的照顧自己，配額只有三分鐘也沒關係。

en.content:
If today you truly can't manage anything,
go push a window open and stand there for three minutes.
Let the air touch your face.
Let the noise outside remind you the world is still turning.
Taking care of yourself doesn't have to mean early mornings, workouts, journaling.
Sometimes it's just this — one lungful of something fresh.
en.editorNote: For the days when even standing up costs something. The lowest-barrier self-care there is, and doing it counts. Good to send yourself, or a friend, during the heaviest part of the afternoon.
variations: If the big thing is out of reach, do the small one. An open window counts.
Today's self-care can be three minutes long and still be self-care.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 AI 情感陪伴工具實測報導談「AI 成為情緒出口」；改寫成半夜對著對話框打字後感到難為情的場景

zh-tw.content:
半夜睡不著，你對著對話框打了一個小時的字。
關掉視窗之後，又覺得自己有點可悲。
可是你看看你剛剛做了什麼——
你把胸口那團說不清楚的東西，
一句一句整理成了話。
那不叫可悲，那叫你還願意照顧自己。
等你有力氣的時候，那些話也會找到人聽。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種半夜找不到人講話、只好對著螢幕說的人。重點不是對誰說，是你願意把情緒說出來。適合在關掉對話視窗、突然覺得空空的那個時刻讀。
variations: 先說得出口，再說給誰聽，順序沒有錯。
把心裡的話整理成句子，本身就是一種自我照顧。

en.content:
You couldn't sleep, so you typed at a chat window for an hour.
Then you closed it and felt a little pathetic.
But look at what you actually just did:
you took the tangled thing in your chest
and turned it, line by line, into words.
That isn't pathetic. That's you still trying to take care of yourself.
When you have the strength, those words will find a person too.
en.editorNote: For the nights when there's no one awake to call, so you talk to a screen instead. What matters isn't who heard it — it's that you got it out. Good to read right after you close the window and the room feels quiet.
variations: Say it out loud first. Finding the right listener can come later.
Turning the mess into sentences is already looking after yourself.

items.sourceNote: 研究指出斷掉習慣後的自責讓人更容易全面放棄，自我疼惜的人反而回得更快；改寫成連續紀錄斷掉一天就整個棄坑的場景

zh-tw.content:
連續三十七天，你每天都有做到。
第三十八天漏掉了，然後你就整個放棄了。
可是你不是回到零，
你是回到第三十七天，中間只是空了一格。
那三十七天不會因為你漏掉一次就消失。
接著做下去就好，不用重來一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種紀錄一斷掉就全面棄坑的人——運動、記帳、語言 app、早睡都算。斷掉之後罵自己的人比較容易放棄，對自己好一點的反而回得快。適合在「反正都斷了」那個念頭冒出來的時候讀。
variations: 空一格，不等於歸零。
中間有洞的紀錄，也還是紀錄。

en.content:
Thirty-seven days in a row, you showed up.
On day thirty-eight you missed, and then you quit entirely.
But you didn't go back to zero.
You went back to day thirty-seven with one gap in the middle.
Those thirty-seven days don't disappear because of one miss.
Just pick it back up. You don't have to start over.
en.editorNote: For anyone who abandons a habit the moment the streak breaks — workouts, budgets, language apps, early nights. People who beat themselves up after a slip quit sooner; people who go easy on themselves come back faster. Read it when "well, it's ruined now" shows up.
variations: A gap is not a reset.
A record with holes in it is still a record.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年心理健康目標文章談「允許休息不必等崩潰」；結合八月颱風季停班停課的台灣情境改寫

zh-tw.content:
颱風天，班停了、店關了，外面的世界暫停半天。
你躺在沙發上才發現：
原來要有人幫你做這個決定，你才敢休息。
不會每次都剛好有颱風替你喊停。
下一次，也許你可以自己說一次：
今天我不要了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個整天明明沒事、卻還是在下午三點打開工作群組把未讀清光的朋友。也適合自己在連續忙了兩個星期、終於躺下來卻渾身不對勁的那個下午讀一次。
variations: 不用等天氣幫你決定，你也可以自己按暫停。
今天不出門，是你發給自己的假單。

en.content:
Typhoon day. Work is called off, the shops are shut, the world outside pauses for half a day.
And lying on the couch you notice:
you only let yourself rest when someone else makes the call.
There won't always be a storm to say it for you.
Maybe next time you can say it yourself —
not today.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend with nothing on all day who still opens the work chat at three in the afternoon to clear the unreads. Also for the afternoon you finally lie down after two solid weeks and can't shake the feeling you should be doing something.
variations: You don't need the weather's permission to pause.
Staying in today is a day off you signed for yourself.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年輕世代消費觀察談「渴望連接」與開口的心理門檻；改寫成太久沒聯絡而不敢傳訊息的場景

zh-tw.content:
有個朋友，你已經半年沒跟他說過話了。
每次想傳訊息，又覺得「現在才傳好像很奇怪」，
然後就再放一個月。
可是關係不會因為安靜就壞掉。
有些人就是這樣：很久沒聯絡，一開口還是原來的樣子。
真的想他的話，傳個貼圖也可以。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種因為隔太久而卡在對話框前面的人。開場白不用完美，先傳出去比較重要。適合在深夜突然想起某個老朋友的時候讀。
variations: 久沒說話，不等於已經不熟了。
一句「欸，突然想到你」，就是很好的開場白。

en.content:
There's a friend you haven't spoken to in six months.
Every time you think about messaging, it feels too late to be normal,
so you put it off another month.
But silence doesn't break a friendship.
Some people are just like that: quiet for ages, then you talk and it's exactly as it was.
If you miss them, a dumb sticker counts as hello.
en.editorNote: For anyone frozen in front of the text box because too much time has passed. The opener doesn't have to be good — sending it matters more. Read it on the night an old friend crosses your mind.
variations: A long silence doesn't mean you've become strangers.
"Hey, you popped into my head today" is a perfectly good opening line.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 15-45 歲免費心理諮商方案報導提到許多人卡在「我的狀況有嚴重到要用嗎」；改寫成預約頁面開著卻按不下送出的場景

zh-tw.content:
預約的頁面你開了三次，最後都關掉。
因為你想：我又沒有很嚴重，這種名額應該留給更需要的人。
可是難受不是比賽，沒有人在幫你的痛苦排名次。
沒有一條線寫著「過了這裡才算數」。
你會一直想按那個按鈕，本身就已經是理由了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種覺得自己「還不夠慘」所以不敢求助的人——諮商、請假、跟朋友開口都算。適合在你已經猶豫很多天、卻還在幫別人保留位子的時候讀。
variations: 痛苦沒有門檻，你不用先夠慘才能被照顧。
你不是在插隊，你只是終於排進去了。

en.content:
You opened the booking page three times and closed it three times.
Because you thought: I'm not that bad, someone else needs this more.
But pain isn't a contest. Nobody is ranking whose hurts more.
There's no line drawn anywhere that says it only counts past here.
The fact that you keep reaching for that button is already reason enough.
en.editorNote: For anyone who won't ask for help because they're "not bad enough" — therapy, a sick day, telling a friend. Read it when you've been hesitating for days while still saving the spot for someone else.
variations: There's no minimum amount of pain required to deserve care.
You're not cutting the line. You finally joined it.

items.sourceNote: 自我疼惜研究指出低潮期的自責會拖慢適應；結合植物換盆後會掉葉的移植適應期改寫成新環境前幾週的脆弱

zh-tw.content:
植物換到大一點的盆子，前兩週一定會掉葉子。
不是你買錯，也不是它撐不住，
是被連根搬動這件事，本來就有代價。
你剛換了工作、換了城市、換了生活的節奏，
這幾週特別容易累、特別想哭，很合理。
先不要急著判定自己選錯了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給剛換環境還在陣痛期的人。新工作、新學校、剛搬家、剛結束一段關係都適用。適合在「我是不是根本不該離開原本那裡」冒出來的第三週讀。
variations: 換盆會掉葉，不代表這盆不該換。
還在適應的你，不是失敗的你。

en.content:
Move a plant into a bigger pot and it will drop leaves for two weeks.
Not because you chose wrong, not because it's weak —
being lifted out by the roots simply costs something.
You just changed jobs, changed cities, changed the shape of your days.
Of course these weeks feel heavy. Of course you're closer to tears.
Don't rush to decide you made a mistake.
en.editorNote: For anyone in the rough stretch right after a change — new job, new school, a move, the end of something. Read it in week three, when "maybe I never should have left" starts talking.
variations: Dropped leaves after repotting don't mean the pot was wrong.
Still adjusting is not the same as failing.

items.sourceNote: 創傷後成長研究指出成長來自個人的因應資源而非創傷本身；改寫成反駁「這些經歷讓你變強大」的安慰話

zh-tw.content:
有人跟你說：「還好有那段經歷，你才變成現在這樣。」
你可以不用點頭。
讓你變成現在這樣的，不是那件事，
是那段時間裡每天還是把自己撿起來的你。
功勞是你的，不是傷你的東西的。
你不需要感謝任何弄痛你的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那些被「吃苦當吃補」式安慰噎到的人。可以在有人叫你「感謝那段經歷」時傳給自己看，也適合陪伴剛走過難關、還沒想原諒的朋友。
variations: 撐過去的是你，不是那件事幫你的。
你可以承認自己長大了，同時不感謝弄傷你的人。

en.content:
Someone tells you, "Well, that's what made you who you are."
You don't have to nod.
What made you who you are wasn't the thing that happened.
It was you, picking yourself up again on every one of those days.
The credit is yours, not the wound's.
You don't owe gratitude to anything that hurt you.
en.editorNote: For anyone tired of being told to be thankful for their worst chapter. Send it to yourself when someone says "everything happens for a reason," or to a friend who just got through something and isn't ready to forgive it.
variations: You carried yourself through it. The hard part didn't do you a favor.
You can admit you grew without thanking what broke you.

items.sourceNote: 2026 情緒趨勢觀察提到「去病理化」與情緒輕量化；改寫成腦內反覆重播舊對話的場景，把反芻正常化

zh-tw.content:
洗澡洗到一半，腦袋突然重播你三年前講錯的那句話，
然後你在蓮蓬頭底下替自己補了一段超完美的回應。
先說：全世界只剩你還記得那件事。
會一直重播，不是你哪裡壞掉了，
是你在乎自己有沒有把人弄傷——這種人通常沒有。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種會被自己過去的社交失誤突襲的人。適合在腦內小劇場又開演的時候讀，提醒自己這是在乎，不是缺陷。可以傳給那個常說「我剛剛是不是講太多」的朋友。
variations: 當事人早就忘了，只有你還在幫他複習。
會反覆回想，是因為你怕傷到人，不是因為你有問題。

en.content:
Mid-shower, your brain replays that thing you said three years ago,
and you deliver a flawless comeback to the showerhead.
First: you are the last person on earth still holding that memory.
And the replaying isn't a malfunction.
It's you checking whether you hurt someone — and people who check usually haven't.
en.editorNote: For anyone ambushed by their own old social slip-ups. Read it when the mental rerun starts again, as a reminder that it's care, not a defect. Good to send to the friend who always asks "was I talking too much?"
variations: They forgot years ago. You're the only one still studying the tape.
You replay it because you're afraid of hurting people, not because something's wrong with you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 nostalgia-as-collective-comfort trend coverage; original writing on comfort rewatching

zh-tw.content:
那部你已經看過三遍的劇，
昨天你又從第一集開始播。
不是沒有新東西可以看，
是你今天沒有力氣再被嚇一次。
知道接下來會發生什麼，本身就是一種安全感。
等你有餘裕了，對新東西的胃口自己會回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個最近一直重看老劇、循環同一張專輯，還為此覺得自己很無趣的朋友。也適合在你按下重播卻有點心虛的晚上，留給自己看。
variations: 重看不是原地踏步，是你替自己挑了一個不會嚇到你的晚上。
今天你需要的不是驚喜，是熟悉。

en.content:
That show you've already seen three times —
last night you started it from episode one again.
It's not that there's nothing new to watch.
It's that today you don't have the energy to be surprised.
Knowing what happens next is its own kind of safety.
When you have room again, the appetite for new things comes back on its own.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps rewatching old shows and looping the same album, then feels boring about it. Also good to keep for the night you hit replay and feel a little guilty about it.
variations: Rewatching isn't standing still. You picked an evening that won't startle you.
Tonight you don't need surprises. You need something familiar.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 wellbeing coverage on digital overload and waiting anxiety; original writing

zh-tw.content:
訊息傳出去兩個小時了，對方還沒回。
這兩個小時裡，你在腦袋裡已經寫完一整齣：
他生氣了、他覺得你很煩、你上次那句話講錯了。
可是沒有回覆不是答案，
那只是還沒有答案而已。
你的腦袋很會填空，而且填進去的幾乎都不是真的。
先去做別的事吧，這一題的答案不在你手上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合等回覆等到坐立難安的時候拿出來看。也可以傳給那個總把別人的安靜解讀成自己做錯事的朋友。
variations: 對方沒回你，通常只代表他在忙，不代表發生了什麼。
等待的時候腦袋自己編的劇情，不能當成證據。

en.content:
You sent the message two hours ago. Still nothing.
In those two hours your head has written a whole script:
he's mad, you're annoying, you shouldn't have said that thing last week.
But no reply isn't an answer.
It's just the absence of one, for now.
Your brain is very good at filling blanks, and almost nothing it fills in is true.
Go do something else. This answer was never yours to write.
en.editorNote: Pull this up when waiting on a reply has you pacing the room. Also good for the friend who reads every silence as proof they did something wrong.
variations: No reply usually means someone is busy, not that something happened.
The story your head wrote while waiting isn't evidence.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 wellness reporting on micro-rest and role fatigue; original writing on the transition pause

zh-tw.content:
你把車停好了，卻沒有馬上下車。
或是走到家門口，先在樓梯間站著發了五分鐘的呆。
那不是懶，也不是不想見家裡的人。
是你在外面當了一整天別人需要的那個角色，
門一打開，又要接著當另一個。
那五分鐘，是今天唯一不必對誰負責的空檔。
你可以留著它，而且不用覺得抱歉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給那些下班到進門之間需要一點空白的人。也可以傳給總覺得自己「連休息都是偷來的」的朋友。
variations: 不用一進門就馬上接班，先給自己一個緩衝。
那五分鐘不是浪費掉的，是你在換氣。

en.content:
You parked the car and didn't get out right away.
Or you reached your door and stood in the stairwell five minutes, looking at nothing.
That's not laziness, and it's not that you don't want to see the people inside.
You spent all day being who everyone out there needed,
and the second that door opens, another shift starts.
Those five minutes are the only stretch of today that belongs to no one.
Keep them. You don't owe anyone an apology for them.
en.editorNote: For anyone who needs a blank gap between clocking out and walking in. Also good for the friend who thinks every break they take is stolen time.
variations: You don't have to clock straight into the next shift. Give yourself a buffer.
Those five minutes aren't wasted. That's you catching your breath.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 Taiwanese wellbeing content on emotional labor; original writing on the designated listener

zh-tw.content:
大家心情不好的時候都會來找你。
你很會問「後來呢」，很會說「這不是你的錯」，
所以沒有人想過要反過來問你一次。
不是他們不在乎，
是你把「我沒事」演得太好了。
你不用等到有人發現，
你也可以先開口說一句：今天換我講。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個總是在聽別人說話、自己的事卻一句都沒提過的朋友。也適合在你覺得「好像沒有人可以說」的那個晚上，留給自己。
variations: 很會接住別人的人，也需要有人接住。
你不用永遠當那個負責安慰的人，今天可以換你被聽。

en.content:
When people are having a bad day, they come to you.
You're good at asking "and then what happened," good at saying "that wasn't your fault" —
so it never occurs to anyone to turn the question around.
It's not that they don't care.
It's that you play "I'm fine" extremely well.
You don't have to wait to be noticed.
You're allowed to say it first: my turn today.
en.editorNote: For the friend who listens to everyone and never mentions their own stuff. Also good to keep for the night you catch yourself thinking there's no one to tell.
variations: The person who catches everyone else needs catching too.
You don't have to be the designated comforter forever. Today you get to be heard.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by longitudinal research on self-criticism vs. psychological flexibility; original writing using GPS rerouting as the frame

zh-tw.content:
你在路口走過頭了，導航沒有嘆氣。
它只說了一句：路線重新規劃中。
它不會倒帶回去檢討你剛剛應該左轉，
它只是從你現在站的這個位置，重新算一次。
你也可以這樣：
不用先開回那個做錯決定的路口，
就從今天的所在地開始重算。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在懊悔某個決定、腦袋一直循環「早知道當初」的時候讀。也可以傳給那個轉職、分手或搬家之後還在回頭檢討自己的朋友。
variations: 你不用回到起點，你只需要從現在這裡開始。
早知道當初沒有用，導航也只認得你現在的位置。

en.content:
You missed the turn, and the GPS didn't sigh at you.
It just said: rerouting.
It doesn't back up to lecture you about the exit you should have taken.
It recalculates from exactly where you are now.
You're allowed to do the same.
You don't have to drive back to the decision you regret.
You can start the math from today's location.
en.editorNote: For the days you're stuck on a choice you'd take back. Good to send to a friend still second-guessing a job, a breakup, or a move.
variations: You don't have to return to the starting point. You only have to start from here.
Hindsight can't route you. Your GPS only works with where you actually are.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 RCT on low-intensity, brief self-compassion practices at work; original writing on the unearned two-minute pause

zh-tw.content:
熱到快融化的下午，你拐進超商，
什麼都沒買，就站在出風口底下吹了兩分鐘。
走出來的時候還有點心虛，好像占了誰的便宜。
可是你只是在被曬垮之前，先幫自己找個地方停一下。
喘一口氣不需要先買點什麼來交換，
也不需要跟誰報備。
你隨時可以按暫停，這件事不用付費。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種連休息都要先幫自己找個正當理由的人。也可以在你只想找個角落待一下、卻覺得自己太懶的午後讀。
variations: 你不用先付出什麼，才換得到一分鐘的涼快。
停下來不用有理由，撐不住本身就是理由。

en.content:
On an afternoon hot enough to melt you, you duck into the convenience store,
buy nothing, and stand under the vent for two minutes.
Walking out, you feel a little guilty, like you took something you didn't pay for.
But all you did was find somewhere to stop before the heat took you down.
Catching your breath doesn't require a purchase,
and it doesn't require explaining yourself to anyone.
You can hit pause anytime. It's free.
en.editorNote: For anyone who needs a valid excuse before they'll rest. Also for the afternoon you just want to sit in a corner for a while and feel lazy about it.
variations: You don't have to earn a minute of cool air.
Stopping doesn't need a reason. Running out of steam is the reason.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 emotional-trend coverage on de-pathologizing and lightweight naming of feelings; original writing on being unable to explain your low mood

zh-tw.content:
有人問你「你到底是為了什麼不開心」，
你張開嘴，發現自己答不出來，
然後開始懷疑自己是不是在無病呻吟。
不是的。
情緒不是申請補助，不用附上理由書和證明文件。
有些日子你只能說「我今天有點糊」，
那樣也算數。
你不必先弄懂自己，才可以難過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在心情低落卻說不出原因的日子讀。也可以傳給那個一難過就先自我審查「我有什麼好難過的」的朋友。
variations: 說不出原因，不代表那份難受是假的。
你不用先寫好一份報告，才可以不舒服。

en.content:
Someone asks what exactly you're upset about,
you open your mouth and realize you can't answer,
and then you start wondering if you're just being dramatic.
You're not.
Feelings aren't a grant application. No supporting documents required.
Some days all you can say is "I'm a little blurry today,"
and that counts.
You don't have to understand yourself before you're allowed to hurt.
en.editorNote: For the low days you can't explain. Send it to the friend who audits their own sadness before letting themselves feel it.
variations: Not being able to name it doesn't make it fake.
You don't owe anyone a report before you're allowed to feel bad.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion literature on agency during distress; original writing on the impulse haircut as a small act of self-direction

zh-tw.content:
你剪掉了留很久的頭髮，
洗完澡擦鏡子的時候還會愣個兩秒。
旁邊的人問你是不是發生了什麼事，
其實也沒有什麼大事，
只是你心裡有個地方想重新開始，
而頭髮是你今天唯一能立刻改變的東西。
那不是衝動，
是你還願意對自己的生活動手，這是好事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在剪短、換髮色或大整理房間之後，被問「你怎麼了」的時候看。也可以傳給那個最近突然很想改變一點什麼的朋友。
variations: 想換個樣子，通常是想換個心情，那沒有不好。
你只是挑了一件今天就能改變的事，從那裡開始也可以。
