en.content:
You cut off hair you'd been growing for years,
and you still pause for two seconds wiping the mirror after a shower.
People ask if something happened.
Nothing dramatic did.
There's just a part of you that wants to start over,
and hair was the one thing you could change today.
That's not impulsive.
That's you still willing to reach into your own life, which is a good sign.
en.editorNote: For after the haircut, the new color, the reorganized room, when someone asks what's going on. Also for the friend who suddenly wants to change something.
variations: Wanting to look different usually means wanting to feel different. Nothing wrong with that.
You picked the one thing you could change today. Starting there counts.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion writing on the disproportionate cost of self-criticism; original writing using forgotten laundry as the frame

zh-tw.content:
你把洗好的衣服忘在洗衣機裡一整晚，
早上打開，那個味道你知道，回不去了。
重洗一次要一個小時。
可是你已經先罵了自己半天，
說什麼「連這種小事都做不好」。
這件事真正的代價，只是一小匙洗衣精。
剩下那些難聽的話，是你自己多加上去的，
而且不用加。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在犯了小錯卻自責到一整天心情很差的時候讀。也可以傳給那個總是把小失誤講成人格問題的朋友。
variations: 很多事的代價只是「再做一次」，不是「你這個人有問題」。
錯誤本身很便宜，是你收自己的利息太高了。

en.content:
You left the wash sitting in the machine all night.
You open it in the morning and you know that smell — it's not coming out.
Running it again costs you an hour.
But you'd already spent half the morning on yourself,
saying things like "I can't even handle this."
The actual price of this mistake was one more scoop of detergent.
Everything else was interest you charged yourself,
and you didn't have to.
en.editorNote: For the day a small slip-up wrecks your whole mood. Send it to the friend who turns every minor mistake into a verdict on their character.
variations: Most mistakes cost you a redo, not your worth.
The error was cheap. The interest you charged yourself wasn't.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by psychology research on social comparison and pace-related stress; original writing using the escalator standing lane as the frame

zh-tw.content:
捷運站的手扶梯，你站在右邊。
左邊一直有人快步超過你，一個接一個，
站著站著，你開始覺得自己是不是太慢了。
可是手扶梯本來就在動。
你站著也在往上，只是沒有用跑的。
上面那層樓不會因為你用走的就關門，
它會等你。
你可以只是站著，讓它把你帶上去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在看到同齡人升遷、結婚、搬新家而覺得自己落後的時候讀。也可以傳給那個最近一直說「我是不是太慢了」的朋友。
variations: 你站著也在往上，只是沒有人幫你配音。
別人用跑的，不代表你用走的就是錯的。

en.content:
On the escalator, you're standing on the right.
People keep striding past on the left, one after another,
and somewhere in there you start wondering if you're too slow.
But the escalator is already moving.
Standing still, you're still going up. You're just not running.
The floor above isn't going to close because you took it at walking pace.
It will wait.
You're allowed to just stand there and let it carry you.
en.editorNote: For when everyone your age seems to be getting promoted, married, or moving into somewhere nicer. Good for the friend who keeps asking if they're behind.
variations: Standing still on a moving stair is still going up.
Someone else running doesn't make your walking pace wrong.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 Taiwanese wellbeing coverage on self-worth after rejection; original writing using the last loaf at closing time as the frame

zh-tw.content:
快打烊的麵包店，架上只剩一個。
它沒有比較不新鮮，也不是烤壞的，
只是今天走進來的每個人，剛好想吃的都不是它。
沒被拿走，跟不好吃，是兩件事。
那份工作、那個人、那個名額也一樣，
他們的挑選，測的是他們今天想要什麼，
不是你值多少。
你還在架上，你還是好的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在面試沒上、告白被拒、或名單裡沒有自己的那天讀。也可以傳給那個開始懷疑「是不是我不夠好」的朋友。
variations: 沒被挑走，只代表今天沒被挑走。
別人的選擇在講他們要什麼，不是在講你值多少。

en.content:
Ten minutes before the bakery closes, one loaf is left on the rack.
It isn't staler than the rest. Nothing went wrong in the oven.
It's just that everyone who walked in today happened to want something else.
Not being picked and not being good are two different facts.
Same with the job, the person, the last spot on the list.
Their choice measures what they wanted today.
It doesn't measure you.
You're still on the rack, and you're still good.
en.editorNote: For the day the interview goes nowhere, the feeling isn't returned, or your name isn't on the list. Send it to the friend starting to think they weren't good enough.
variations: Not chosen today only means not chosen today.
Someone's pick describes their appetite, not your value.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by writing on boundaries and voicing needs; original writing using customized bubble tea orders as the frame

zh-tw.content:
點手搖的時候你會說：微糖、少冰、不要加料。
說得很順，也沒有覺得自己很難搞。
可是換成人，你就開始吞回去了。
「這樣講會不會太計較」「算了，忍一下就過去」。
你對一杯飲料都願意講清楚你要什麼，
對自己的生活更可以。
說出需求不是找麻煩，
那只是讓別人知道要怎麼對你好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個什麼都說「都可以」、回家再自己難過的朋友。也適合在你想開口卻又硬吞下去的那個當下讀。
variations: 你對飲料都能講清楚，對人也可以。
講出你要什麼，不是難搞，是省得大家都在猜。

en.content:
Ordering tea, you say it without blinking: half sugar, light ice, no boba.
It's easy. You don't feel high-maintenance about it.
But with people, you swallow it back down.
"Is that too picky?" "Never mind, I'll just deal with it."
You'll spell out exactly what you want from a drink.
You're allowed to do that with your life.
Saying what you need isn't being difficult.
It's telling people how to be good to you.
en.editorNote: For the friend who answers "anything's fine" and then feels bad about it at home. Also for the moment you're about to swallow something you meant to say.
variations: If you can specify it for a drink, you can specify it for a person.
Naming what you want isn't difficult. It saves everyone the guessing.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 Taiwanese coverage of 療癒宅 trends emphasizing comfort and small decompression corners; original writing using the un-lit living room at dusk as the frame

zh-tw.content:
夏末的週日晚上，天黑得比上個月早了十幾分鐘。
你坐在客廳，還沒開燈，
才發現屋子裡的光是慢慢退掉的，不是誰把它關掉的。
沒有人宣布過夏天結束了，
它只是一天暗一點點。
你想要的那些改變也可以這樣，
不用挑一個日子、不用先跟誰交代，
慢慢換過去就好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個把「下個月一號再開始」講了三次的朋友。也適合自己在剛換季、從衣櫃深處翻出長袖那天晚上讀一次。
variations: 季節換的時候沒有敲鑼打鼓，你要變成什麼樣子，也不用先公告。
不用等一個新的月份、新的星期一。今天暗了一點點，就已經在換了。

en.content:
Late-summer Sunday evenings go dark about fifteen minutes earlier than last month's did.
You're sitting in the living room with the lights still off,
and you notice the light didn't get switched off — it drained out slowly.
Nobody announced that summer was over.
It just got a little darker each day.
The changes you want can happen that way too:
no start date, nothing to announce,
just one shade different, and then another.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who has said "I'll start on the first of next month" three times now. Also good to read on the evening you pull the long sleeves back out of the closet.
variations: Seasons turn without an announcement. So can you.
You don't need a Monday for this. One shade different today already counts.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by research on distress after relationship endings and the pacing of recovery; original writing reframing the detour route as a legitimate choice rather than a stalled recovery

zh-tw.content:
有一條路，你已經很久沒有走了。
每次都多繞五分鐘，繞到自己都覺得有點好笑。
可是繞路不是你還沒好起來的證據，
那只是你決定，今天的力氣不要花在那裡。
總有一天你會不小心走過去，走到一半才想起來，
而且不會有人發獎狀給你。
在那之前，繞著走也是一條回家的路。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個為了避開前公司樓下那間便利商店、每天多走五分鐘卻不好意思說的人。也適合自己被問「你怎麼還沒走出來」的那天看一次。
variations: 你不是在繞路，你是在選一條今天走得完的路。
哪天你走到一半才想起來，那才叫好了。在那之前，繞著走很好。

en.content:
There's a street you haven't walked down in months.
You add five minutes to the trip every single time, and by now it feels a little absurd.
But going around isn't evidence that you're still broken.
It's you deciding where today's energy gets spent.
Some day you'll be halfway down it before you even remember,
and nobody will hand you a certificate for it.
Until then, the long way is still a way home.
en.editorNote: For the person walking five extra minutes daily to avoid the shop under their old office and feeling silly about it. Also for the day someone asks why you're not over it yet.
variations: The long way isn't a detour. It's the route you can actually finish today.
One day you'll be halfway down it before it registers. Until then, go around.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by a systematic review of self-compassion interventions and wellbeing outcomes; original writing using the bowl-instead-of-the-pot dinner as the frame

zh-tw.content:
其實直接端著鍋子吃也可以，反正沒有人會知道。
但你還是拿了一個碗，
把桌上的東西挪開，坐下來，好好吃完。
沒有人看見，這件事還是成立。
因為你心裡有一塊地方，
把自己算成一個值得被招待的客人。
那塊地方是對的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一個人住的第一年，煮完麵站在流理台前面猶豫「要不要多洗一個碗」的那三秒。也可以傳給剛搬出來自己住的朋友。
variations: 只有你在的時候，你還是拿了碗。這件小事沒有你以為的那麼小。
你把自己當客人招待了一次，那個人值得再被這樣招待很多次。

en.content:
Eating straight out of the pot would have been fine. Nobody would ever have known.
You got a bowl anyway.
Cleared the mail off the table, sat down, finished it like an actual meal.
No one saw it. It still counts.
Somewhere in you there's a part
that counts you as a guest worth setting a table for.
That part is right.
en.editorNote: For the first year of living alone — those three seconds at the counter deciding whether one more bowl is worth washing. Send it to a friend who just moved into a place of their own.
variations: You reached for the bowl with nobody watching. That isn't a small thing.
You set a table for yourself once. That person deserves it again tomorrow.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 research writing on cognitive load and unfinished tasks; original writing on the urge to tidy a drawer when the real problem can't be solved

zh-tw.content:
心情爛到谷底的那天，你沒有躺著，
反而蹲在地上開始整理抽屜。
你覺得自己有點好笑，
但那不是逃避。
真正麻煩的那件事修不好的時候，
手會自己去找一件做得完的事。
整理好的那格抽屜不會解決什麼，
它只是今天唯一有照你的話做的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個吵完架不講話、卻默默把整個廚房擦乾淨的家人。也適合自己在半夜莫名其妙開始整理衣櫃的時候看。
variations: 大的那件事動不了的時候，手會自己去找一件做得完的。
抽屜整齊了也不會怎樣，它只是今天唯一聽你話的東西。

en.content:
Worst day in weeks, and instead of lying down
you're crouched on the floor sorting out a drawer.
It feels slightly ridiculous.
It isn't avoidance.
When the thing that actually hurts can't be fixed,
your hands go looking for something that can be finished.
The drawer solves nothing, and it was never meant to.
It's just the one piece of today that did what you asked.
en.editorNote: For the family member who goes quiet after an argument and silently scrubs the entire kitchen. Also for you, at midnight, reorganizing a closet for no reason you can name.
variations: When the big thing won't budge, your hands go find something that will.
A tidy drawer fixes nothing. It's just the one thing today that cooperated.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion writing on tolerating uncertainty; camera-focus metaphor written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
想拍下什麼的時候，鏡頭會先來回抓兩下，
畫面糊掉、清楚、又糊回去，
然後才停在該停的地方。
沒有人會在那一秒罵手機壞掉，
大家都知道它正在對焦。
你現在也是。
你不是拍不出來，你只是還沒對到焦。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給剛畢業、剛離職、或說不出自己到底想要什麼的朋友。也適合自己在「別人好像都很清楚，只有我一片模糊」的那種晚上看。
variations: 畫面糊掉不是壞掉，是還在對焦。
先讓自己糊一陣子，清楚會自己來。

en.content:
Point a camera at something and the lens hunts—
blurry, sharp, blurry again,
before it settles where it should.
Nobody yells at the phone for being broken.
Everyone knows it's just focusing.
So are you.
You're not failing to see it. You're mid-focus.
en.editorNote: For the friend who just graduated, just quit, or can't put into words what they actually want. Also for you, on the night when everyone else seems to have a sharp picture and yours is a smear.
variations: A blurry frame isn't a broken lens. It's a focusing one.
Let yourself be out of focus a while. Sharp arrives on its own.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by stress-management writing on rumination and stepping away from a problem; burnt-pan metaphor written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
鍋底燒焦的那天，你越用力刷，它越花。
後來才學會：先加水，放著，去做別的事。
一個小時後回來，輕輕一推就掉了。
有些事情也是這樣。
現在拚命想通、拚命處理，
只會在自己身上多刮出幾道痕。
先泡著吧。
放著不動不是不管它，是在等它自己鬆開。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給正在為一件事反覆鑽牛角尖、每天都想「一次講清楚」的朋友。也適合自己半夜又要點開那段對話紀錄之前，先看一次。
variations: 越用力刷越花，先加水泡著吧。
放著不動不是不管它，是在等它自己鬆開。

en.content:
The day you burn a pan, scrubbing harder only scratches it.
Eventually you learn: add water, walk away, do something else.
Come back an hour later and it lifts off with one push.
Some things work the same way.
Forcing yourself to solve it tonight
just leaves marks on you.
Let it soak.
Leaving it alone isn't neglect. It's waiting for it to loosen by itself.
en.editorNote: For the friend circling the same problem every day, sure that one more perfectly worded conversation will settle it. Also for you, right before you reopen that thread at 1 a.m.
variations: Scrub harder and you only scratch it. Add water instead.
Leaving it alone isn't neglect. It's waiting for it to loosen.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 consumer reporting on subscription creep and buried cancel buttons; reframed as a metaphor for commitments that quietly drain energy

zh-tw.content:
每年總有一天，你會在帳單裡翻到那一筆，
一個扣了很久、你卻半年沒打開過的服務。
不是你笨，是取消的那顆按鈕本來就藏得很深。
你的力氣也有這種東西：
一個從來不會安靜的群組、
一個每次見完都讓你變小一點的人、
一場你早就不想去的聚會。
它們每個月都在扣，只是不會寄帳單來提醒你。
今年可以退訂一個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在月底對帳、或年初整理人際關係的時候看。也適合傳給那個老是說「不好意思拒絕」的朋友。
variations: 會扣你力氣的東西，不會寄帳單來提醒你。
今年退訂一個吧，從那個每次見完都更累的約開始。

en.content:
Once a year you scroll the statement and find it:
something you haven't opened in six months, still billing away.
You're not careless. They bury the cancel button on purpose.
Your energy has these too.
The group chat that never goes quiet.
The person you shrink around.
The standing plan you stopped wanting years ago.
They charge you every month and never send a statement.
You're allowed to cancel one this year.
en.editorNote: For the end of the month when you're reconciling accounts, or the start of a year when you're reconciling people. Also for the friend whose whole personality is not knowing how to say no.
variations: The things that drain you don't send a monthly statement.
Cancel one this year. Start with the plan you dread all week.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by writing on attachment to sentimental objects and identity; old-key scene and closing reframe written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
鑰匙圈上有一把，你已經想不起來是開哪一扇門的。
每次整理都拿起來看兩秒，然後又串回去。
留著它，不代表你還走不出來。
那扇門後面曾經是你的生活——
有你的味道、你的杯子、你可以放心睡著的地方。
會捨不得，是因為它真的存在過。
哪天你想丟，不用等到自己完全不在意了才有資格丟；
哪天你不丟，也沒有人規定鑰匙圈上
只能掛用得到的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給剛搬離舊家、剛結束一段關係，或是收東西收到一半就坐在地上發呆的朋友。
variations: 留著那把鑰匙，不代表你還站在門口等。
捨不得，只是因為它真的存在過。

en.content:
There's a key on your ring and you no longer know what it opens.
Every time you sort through things you hold it, think, and thread it back.
Keeping it doesn't mean you're stuck.
Behind that door was a life that was genuinely yours—
your smell, your mug, the place you fell asleep without checking the lock.
It's hard to throw out because it was real.
If you toss it someday, you don't have to wait
until it means nothing before you're allowed to.
And if you never do, no rule says a keyring
may only carry keys you use.
en.editorNote: For the friend who just moved out, just ended something, or is sitting on the floor halfway through a box they meant to pack.
variations: Keeping the key doesn't mean you're still waiting at the door.
It's hard to let go because it was real. That's the whole reason.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion writing practice on staying with slow, invisible progress; tap-water scene and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
洗碗的時候你把熱水轉到底，
流出來的還是冰的。
水管裡那一段冷水，總得先走完。
那幾十秒不是壞掉，也不是白流。
你最近開始做的那些小事——
早一點放下手機、多走兩站路、
把想講的話真的講出口——
現在感覺不到差別，很正常。
不是沒有用，
是熱的那一段還在路上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給最近開始改變一點生活習慣、卻覺得「好像沒什麼用」而想放棄的朋友。
variations: 一開始流出來的是冷水，不代表水龍頭壞了。
感覺不到差別的那幾十秒，最需要的是先別關掉。

en.content:
You turn the tap all the way to hot and it still runs cold.
There's a stretch of cold sitting in the pipe that has to clear out first.
Those thirty seconds aren't a malfunction, and they aren't wasted.
The small things you started doing lately—
putting the phone down earlier, walking one stop further,
actually saying the thing out loud—
of course you can't feel a difference yet.
It isn't that they don't work.
The warm part is still on its way.
en.editorNote: For the friend who started something small a couple weeks ago and is about to quit because nothing feels different yet.
variations: Cold water first doesn't mean the tap is broken.
The stretch where you feel nothing is the stretch where you don't turn it off.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by writing on self-blame over everyday forgetfulness and mental load; lost-transit-card scene and reframe written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
出門前找不到悠遊卡，
整個包倒出來、抽屜翻兩遍、連沙發縫都摸過，
最後在昨天那件外套口袋裡。
你一路走去車站，一路唸自己怎麼這麼會忘東西。
可是你也可以這樣想：
那天早上你腦袋裡同時開著十幾個視窗——
誰在等你回訊息、幾點要出門、晚餐買什麼，
卡片只是被擠到最後一個。
記性不是你的人品，
只是你今天實在裝了太多事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給最近老是忘東忘西、然後開始懷疑「我是不是哪裡有問題」的朋友。
variations: 你不是變笨了，是同時開太多視窗。
忘東忘西不代表你不用心，只代表你的腦袋今天太滿了。

en.content:
You can't find your transit card on the way out.
You dump the whole bag, go through two drawers, feel down the side of the couch—
it was in yesterday's jacket.
You walk to the station calling yourself scatterbrained the whole way.
Here's another way to read it:
your head had a dozen windows open that morning—
who's waiting on a reply, what time you have to leave, what's for dinner—
and the card got pushed to the back of the stack.
Forgetting things isn't a character flaw.
Some days you're just carrying too much at once.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps misplacing things lately and has started wondering if something is wrong with them.
variations: You didn't get dumber. You just have too many windows open.
Forgetting things doesn't mean you don't care. It means your head is full.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by reflections on people who habitually caretake and stay out of frame; group-photo scene and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
聚餐要結束的時候，大家喊「來拍一張」，
拿手機的又是你。
那天晚上你把相簿往回翻，
翻了三年，幾乎都是別人笑得很開心的樣子。
你不是不想入鏡，
只是每次都習慣先退到後面，
把好位置留給大家。
下次可以試著把手機遞出去，
說一句「幫我拍一張」。
那不是搶鏡頭，
是你也在那個晚上，本來就應該看得見。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個總是負責拍照、負責訂位、負責照顧大家的朋友。
variations: 每次都退到鏡頭後面的人，也該被拍進去。
「幫我拍一張」不是麻煩別人，是你也在場的證據。

en.content:
Dinner's wrapping up, someone says let's get a photo,
and you're the one holding the phone again.
That night you scroll back through your camera roll—
three years of it, almost all other people laughing.
It's not that you don't want to be in the frame.
You just step back by reflex
and leave the good spot for everyone else.
Next time, try handing the phone over
and saying, take one with me in it.
That isn't hogging the shot.
You were there that night too. It should show.
en.editorNote: For the friend who always takes the picture, books the table, and looks after everyone else first.
variations: The person who always steps behind the camera belongs in the photo too.
"Take one with me in it" isn't a favor. It's proof you were there.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by healing-drama lines about being quietly remembered; noodle-shop scene and reframe written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
轉角那家麵攤，你去了大概兩年。
那天你還沒開口，老闆先說了一句：
「不要香菜齁。」
你笑一笑坐下來，心裡卻有點想哭。
你常覺得自己在哪裡都不太重要，
可是有人把你這種小到不行的事記了下來。
被記得不需要你很出色，
也不用你先變成更好的誰。
你只是來過、坐過、說過一次話，
就已經在別人那裡留下位置了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給最近覺得自己「對誰來說都可有可無」的朋友，也適合低潮的晚上自己重看一次。
variations: 有人記得你不吃香菜，那也是一種被放在心上。
你不用很出色，才值得被記得。

en.content:
The noodle shop on the corner—you've been going about two years.
That day, before you said anything, the owner called out:
no cilantro, right?
You laughed and sat down, and something in your chest went tight.
You spend a lot of time feeling like you don't much matter anywhere,
and yet somebody filed away a detail that small about you.
Being remembered doesn't require you to be impressive.
It doesn't wait until you've become a better version of yourself.
You showed up, sat down, said a few words once—
and that already left a space with your name on it.
en.editorNote: For the friend who's been feeling replaceable lately, and for your own rereading on a low night.
variations: Someone remembering you hate cilantro is someone keeping you in mind.
You don't have to be impressive to be worth remembering.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 lunar-seventh-month guides that include a simplified version for renters and small households; rented-room scene and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
農曆七月，老家傳了照片到家族群組：
桌子搬到門口，供品擺了兩層，該有的都有。
你這邊呢，套房裡沒有神明桌，
樓下管理室的紅紙上寫著禁止焚燒。
你只在下班路上買了一包餅乾，
拆開之前，在心裡先講了兩句話。
那樣就不算數嗎？
你沒有把上一代的每一個步驟都留下來，
可是你記得這個時候要買什麼、要說什麼、要想起誰。
形式會被房子的大小改掉，
你放在心上的那部分不會。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合這個月回不了老家、或第一次自己在外面過農曆七月的人；也適合傳給覺得自己沒把家裡那套規矩接下來的朋友。
variations: 你沒有照著做每一個步驟，不代表你把那些人忘了。
在心裡念過一次，也是一種到了。

en.content:
Two tiers of offerings, the table dragged out to the doorway—the photo lands in the family group chat.
Your place has no altar. The notice by the mailboxes says nothing may be burned in the building.
So you bought a pack of cookies on the way home,
and before opening it, said a couple of things in your head.
Does that not count?
You didn't keep every step the generation before you kept.
You did remember what to buy this time of year, what to say, who to think about.
The form gets edited by how big your apartment is.
The part you carry doesn't.
en.editorNote: For anyone spending this month far from the family house, or marking it alone in a rented room for the first time.
variations: Skipping the steps isn't the same as forgetting the people.
Saying it in your head still counts as saying it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by reporting on connection being something felt rather than counted; library-marginalia scene and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
借回來的書翻到一半，
發現有人用鉛筆在某一段旁邊畫了一條很淡的線。
那個人不認識你，
也不會知道你今天剛好很需要那一段。
你這一年也做過幾件那樣的事——
幫誰講了一句話、傳了一則不要求回覆的訊息、
在某個人很難的那天多留了十分鐘。
沒有人回頭告訴你那些有沒有用，
所以你以為都沒落到誰身上。
可是你給出去的東西不會寄回執，
它只是安靜地留在別人的某一頁上，
在你早就忘記的時候，被翻開。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種默默對人很好、卻常常覺得自己沒幫上什麼忙的朋友。
variations: 沒有回音，不等於沒有到達。
你留下的那條線，會在你忘記以後被誰翻到。

en.content:
A faint pencil line beside one paragraph, halfway through a library book.
Whoever drew it doesn't know you,
and will never know you needed that paragraph today.
You did a few things like that this year—
spoke up for someone, sent a message that asked for nothing back,
stayed ten extra minutes on a day that was hard for somebody else.
Nobody reported back on whether any of it helped,
so you filed it all under wasted.
What you give out doesn't come with a delivery receipt.
It sits quietly on someone else's page,
and gets opened long after you've forgotten leaving it.
en.editorNote: For the friend who is quietly good to people and assumes none of it ever registers.
variations: No reply doesn't mean it never arrived.
The line you left gets found long after you forget leaving it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by a Taiwanese counselor's piece on constant self-monitoring and self-compassion practice; worn-shirt scene and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
衣櫃裡那件洗到領口鬆掉的舊衣服，
你不會穿它出門，也不會穿它去見任何人。
可是一回到家，你伸手拿的還是它。
因為它不會要求你站直、收小腹、看起來像個樣子。
有些關係也是這種質地：
拿不出去給人看，但你在裡面可以整個人放下來。
你不需要二十四小時都維持在可以見人的那個版本。
被看見很重要，
有地方讓你不用被看見，也一樣重要。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合下班回家已經沒力氣再應付任何人的晚上，也適合傳給那個在外面很得體、只有回家才鬆得下來的朋友。
variations: 有地方可以不用被看見，也是一種被照顧。
那件不能穿出門的衣服，是你家裡最舒服的東西。

en.content:
Stretched-out collar, washed soft, shoved to one side of the closet.
You'd never wear it out. You'd never wear it to meet anyone.
Come home, though, and it's the first thing your hand finds.
It doesn't ask you to stand straighter or look like someone who has it together.
Some relationships have that same texture:
not presentable, but you can put your whole weight down inside them.
You don't have to hold the presentable version of yourself twenty-four hours a day.
Being seen matters.
Having somewhere you don't have to be seen matters just as much.
en.editorNote: For nights when you're out of energy for other people, and for the friend who is polished all day and only unclenches at home.
variations: Somewhere you don't have to be seen is its own kind of care.
The shirt you'd never wear out is the most comfortable thing you own.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by commentary on wanting company and where a sense of being cared for actually comes from; holiday-week scene and the roommate/coworker/phone-call details written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
這幾天花店門口開始擺出成束的花，
手機也自動推播起兩個人才用得到的優惠。
一年就這麼幾天在講愛，
沒有對象的人好像自動被算在外面。
可是你回頭數這一年真正撐住你的：
是室友幫你留到半夜的那盞燈，
是同事看你臉色不對，什麼都沒問就先倒了一杯水給你，
是很久沒聯絡的朋友接起電話，第一句是「你先講」。
這些都不會被算進節日裡，
可是它們都是有人在乎你的證據。
愛沒有規定要用哪一種身分送到，
只是要有人願意。
而你今年，已經被這樣對待過很多次了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合節日前後覺得自己被排除在外的人，也適合傳給那個「沒有另一半就覺得自己少了什麼」的朋友。
variations: 不是只有戀愛，才算被好好對待。
替你留燈、倒水、接電話的那些人，也在那份名單上。

en.content:
Bundles of flowers appear outside the shop this week, and your phone starts pushing deals built for two.
A handful of days a year get to be about love,
and if nobody's waiting for you, it can feel like you were left off the list.
Count back over this year at what actually held you up:
the roommate who left a light on past midnight,
the coworker who read your face, asked nothing, and set a glass of water down,
the friend you hadn't called in months who picked up and said, you go first.
None of that gets counted on a holiday.
All of it is evidence somebody meant it.
Love doesn't come with rules about which relationship gets to deliver it.
Somebody just has to be willing—and this year, plenty of people were.
en.editorNote: For anyone feeling left off the list around a couples' holiday, and for the friend who thinks being single means something is missing.
variations: Romance isn't the only thing that counts as being loved well.
The people who left a light on for you belong on that list too.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion writing on self-kindness and knowing your own needs; salon-chair dialogue and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
「今天想剪什麼樣子？」
「都可以，你看著弄。」
說完你就把手機拿起來，怕再被問下去。
不是不在意，是你真的不知道要回什麼。
選餐廳配別人的口味，排假配別人的行程，
每次都選那個對大家比較方便的方案，
久到「你想要什麼」變成一個你答不出來的題目。
下次先不要急著說都可以。
就算只回一句「不要剪太短」也好。
那不是任性，
是你把自己重新放回可以被選的那一邊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給點餐、選餐廳、排假都習慣說「都可以」的朋友；也適合最近覺得自己好像沒什麼喜好的人自己看。
variations: 「都可以」講久了，連自己想要什麼都會忘記。
說出一個小小的偏好，就是把自己放回選項裡。

en.content:
"So what are we doing today?"
"Whatever you think. You decide."
Then you pick up your phone so nobody asks again.
It's not that you don't care. You genuinely don't know what to say.
Years of picking the restaurant someone else likes, taking the days off that suit everyone else,
choosing whichever option was easier on the group—
long enough that what do you want became a question you can't answer.
Next time, don't reach for whatever straight away.
Even just: nothing too short.
That isn't being difficult.
That's putting yourself back among the things that get chosen.
en.editorNote: For the friend who answers "whatever you want" to every restaurant, every plan, every decision.
variations: Say "whatever" long enough and you forget what you actually wanted.
Naming one small preference puts you back on the list of options.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by burnout-recovery writing on discounting your own effort; the week's list of small completed things written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
你說這星期什麼都沒做。
可是：
你把積了三天的碗洗完了。
你點開了那封一直不敢看的信。
你跟一個人說了「這次我沒辦法」。
你在最想放棄的那天，還是把自己弄去上班了。
這些沒有一項會出現在待辦清單上，
因為清單只記得你還沒做完的。
剩下的那些，得由你自己來記。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合週日晚上覺得「這星期又白過了」的時候拿出來看，也適合傳給總是低估自己的朋友。
variations: 待辦清單只記得你沒做完的，不會記得你撐過的。
沒有被打勾的那些，也是你做到的事。

en.content:
You say you did nothing this week.
Except:
you washed the dishes that had been sitting for three days.
you opened the email you'd been avoiding.
you told someone, I can't take this one.
and on the day you most wanted to quit, you still got yourself to work.
None of that shows up on a to-do list,
because a list only keeps track of what's unfinished.
The rest of it, you'll have to count yourself.
en.editorNote: For Sunday nights that feel like a wasted week, and for the friend who always undercounts what they got through.
variations: A to-do list remembers what you didn't finish, never what you survived.
The things with no checkbox still count as done.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by a Taiwanese counselor's notes on emotions accumulating when unspoken; dehumidifier-tank scene and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
房間裡的除濕機又在嗶了。
你拉出水箱，滿滿一整格，
明明前幾天才倒過。
空氣裡的潮濕不會自己消失，
它只是慢慢地、一點一點被機器接住。
你也一樣。
那些沒地方說的話、忍下來的委屈、
不好意思麻煩別人的那一部分，
不會因為你沒提就不存在，
只是先裝在一個你看不到的地方。
偶爾也要記得拉出來倒一倒。
不是你太脆弱，
是任何東西滿了都會響。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合最近動不動就情緒滿出來、又不好意思找人講的時候；也適合傳給習慣什麼都自己吞的朋友。
variations: 滿了會響不是壞掉，是在叫你倒一倒。
你沒說出口的那些，不會因為沒說就不見。

en.content:
The dehumidifier in your room is beeping again.
You pull the tank out—full to the line,
and you emptied it only a few days ago.
The damp in the air doesn't disappear on its own.
It just gets caught, slowly, a little at a time.
Same with you.
The things you had nowhere to say, the unfairness you swallowed,
the part of you that didn't want to be a burden:
none of it stops existing because you kept quiet.
It collects somewhere you can't see.
Pull it out and pour it away now and then.
You're not fragile.
Anything beeps when it's full.
en.editorNote: For when your feelings keep spilling over and you don't want to bother anyone, and for the friend who swallows everything alone.
variations: Beeping when it's full isn't broken. It's asking to be emptied.
What you never said out loud didn't go anywhere.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion writing on judging your whole self by one failing; shoe-repair scene and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
鞋子拿去修，師傅翻來翻去看了看，說：
「這雙底還很好，換個跟就可以再穿很久。」
你其實已經打算丟了。
壞掉的那一小塊，不等於整雙的價值。
你也不是不能用了，
你只是有一個地方，需要有人幫忙換掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合覺得自己「已經沒救了」的時候；也適合傳給正在為一個缺點全盤否定自己的朋友。
variations: 一個地方壞了，不代表整個都要丟。
需要修的是一個部分，不是你整個人。

en.content:
You take the shoes in. The repairman turns them over a few times.
Soles are still good, he says. New heels and you'll get years out of these.
You'd already decided to throw them out.
The part that broke isn't the worth of the whole thing.
You're not past using either.
There's just one piece of you that needs somebody's help replacing.
en.editorNote: For when you've written yourself off entirely, and for the friend condemning all of themselves over one flaw.
variations: One part failing doesn't mean the whole thing gets thrown out.
What needs fixing is a piece of you, not all of you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Taiwanese mental-health guidance on shifting bedtime gradually before a long break ends; wording and framing written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
別要求自己今晚就睡好。
先早十五分鐘躺下，
剩下的交給幾天以後。
zh-tw.editorNote: 暑假快結束、要早起的日子又要回來的時候看。
variations: 作息不是一個晚上壞掉的，也不會一個晚上調回來。
今天早十五分鐘，就已經在調了。

en.content:
Don't ask yourself to sleep well tonight.
Just get into bed fifteen minutes earlier.
Leave the rest to a few days from now.
en.editorNote: For the end of a long break, when early mornings are coming back.
variations: Your sleep didn't break in one night. It won't come back in one either.
Fifteen minutes earlier today already counts as fixing it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion research on self-kindness and receiving warmth; compliment-deflecting scene written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
被誇的時候，先不要急著說沒有啦。
試著只回一句謝謝，
然後讓那句話留在身上久一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次被稱讚都馬上否認的朋友。
variations: 說謝謝不是驕傲，只是讓好話有地方放。
別人看見你的好，你可以先不要幫他反駁。

en.content:
When someone compliments you, don't rush to wave it off.
Try just saying thank you,
and let it sit on you a while.
en.editorNote: For the friend who deflects every compliment within half a second.
variations: Saying thank you isn't arrogance. It just gives the kind words somewhere to land.
When someone sees something good in you, you don't have to argue them out of it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by continuing-bonds writing on everyday reminders keeping a connection alive; supermarket scene and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
你以為想念會一直是痛的，
後來它慢慢變成一種習慣。
在超市看到他以前愛吃的那個牌子，
手會停一下；
經過那家店，你會在心裡跟他講一句話。
那不是你還沒走出來。
是那個人換了一種方式，
繼續留在你每天會經過的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合這個月想起某個不在了的人的時候，一個人看。
variations: 想念沒有消失，只是換了一個比較安靜的樣子。
會想起來，就表示那個人真的在你這裡住過。

en.content:
You thought missing someone would stay sharp.
Instead it turned into a habit.
The brand they liked, spotted in a supermarket aisle—your hand pauses.
Walking past a certain shop, you say something to them in your head.
That isn't being stuck.
It's that they've changed form,
and stayed in the places you pass every day.
en.editorNote: For a month when someone who's gone keeps coming to mind. Read it alone.
variations: The missing didn't leave. It just got quieter.
If they still come to mind, they really did live here with you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion writing on guilt after snapping at people closest to you; phone-call scene and closing lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
家裡打來問你吃飽沒，
你回得很短，講沒兩句就說要忙。
掛掉之後，你有點討厭自己。
可是在外面你整天都在挑字、看臉色、把語氣修得剛剛好，
只有對他們，你才敢用完全沒力氣的聲音講話。
那不是不愛，那是你放心。
然後，晚一點再傳一句過去，也永遠來得及。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合對最親的人不小心兇了以後，坐在那裡難受的時候。
variations: 會對最親的人露出最累的樣子，是因為你在他們面前不用演。
晚一點補一句話，還是算數的。

en.content:
They call to ask if you've eaten.
You answer in three words and say you're busy.
After you hang up, you don't like yourself much.
But all day out there you pick your words, read faces, sand your tone down smooth.
They get the voice you have nothing left to spend on.
That isn't a lack of love. That's you off guard.
And a message sent later still lands.
en.editorNote: For sitting in the bad feeling after being short with the people closest to you.
variations: You show your most tired face to the people you don't have to perform for.
Sending it a few hours late still counts.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by burnout writing on unrealistic daily workloads; to-do list scene and lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
待辦清單上那三件事，放到明天也不會壞掉。
今天先讓自己喘一口氣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合下班還在盯著清單、覺得自己不夠快的晚上。
variations: 清單不會因為你今天休息一下就長出腳跑掉。
先把自己顧好，再回來處理那些等得起的事。

en.content: Those three things on your list won't spoil by tomorrow. Give yourself today to just breathe.
en.editorNote: For a night when you're off work but still staring at the list.
variations: The list isn't going to grow legs and run off because you rested.
Take care of yourself first. The patient things can wait.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by stress-management writing on problems that need time rather than force; phrasing written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
有些事不是你今天想不通，
是它本來就需要更久一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合為了一個想不出答案的問題卡了一整天的時候。
variations: 想不出來不代表你笨，可能只是時間還沒到。
有些結，要放著幾天才會自己鬆一點。

en.content: Some things aren't unsolvable today. They simply need longer than one day.
en.editorNote: For a day spent stuck on a question that won't resolve.
variations: Not figuring it out doesn't mean you're slow. It might just be early.
Some knots only loosen after a few days of being left alone.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by everyday stress-management writing on urgency framing; wording written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
把「現在馬上」改成「這週某一天」，
天不會塌下來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個把每件事都排成急件的人。
variations: 不是每件事都掛急診，大部分都可以排隊。
換一個期限，你會發現世界照樣運轉。

en.content: Swap "right now" for "sometime this week." The sky stays up.
en.editorNote: For the person who files every task as urgent.
variations: Not everything is an emergency. Most things can take a number.
Move the deadline and watch the world keep running.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by writing on rest and decision-making capacity; lines written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
不是每件事都要今天有答案。
有些答案要等你睡飽才會出現。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜還在腦內開會、決定不了的時候。
variations: 累到不行的時候做的決定，通常都不算數。
先去睡，明天的你比現在的你聰明一點。

en.content: Not everything needs an answer today. Some answers only show up after you've slept.
en.editorNote: For 2 a.m., when your brain is still holding a meeting.
variations: Decisions made on an empty tank rarely hold up in the morning.
Go to sleep. Tomorrow's version of you is sharper than this one.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 zh-tw coverage of 隱性焦慮 (being tense without an obvious cause); instrument-tuning analogy written original for this collection

zh-tw.content:
木頭做的樂器，放著沒動也會走音。
不是誰去碰了它，
是空氣一直在變，它就跟著鬆一點、緊一點。
會被影響，是因為它是活的。
你最近比較容易煩、比較沒力氣，
先不要當成自己退步了。
調一調就好，不用換掉整把。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合最近狀態變差、開始懷疑「我是不是變糟了」的人。把「壞掉」翻譯成「走音」，聽起來就沒那麼嚴重了。
variations: 會隨環境變化的東西，通常都是活的。你也是。
狀態不好不等於本質壞掉，多數時候只是需要重新調一次。

en.content: A wooden instrument goes out of tune even when nobody touches it. The air keeps changing, so the strings sit a little looser, a little tighter. It reacts because it's made of something alive. If you've been more irritable and slower lately, that isn't proof you're getting worse. Tune it. You don't need a new instrument.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose recent dip has them wondering if they're fundamentally broken. Reframing 'broken' as 'out of tune' takes most of the weight off.
variations: Anything that responds to its environment is alive. That includes you.
A bad stretch isn't a defect. Usually it just means it's time to retune.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 zh-tw writing on emotional self-care and endlessly deferred needs; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
你把很多事情都排在「等我忙完這陣子」後面。
想約的那杯咖啡、想去看的那科醫生、想回的那通電話。
可是這陣子，已經連著好幾年了。
它不是一個真的會到的日期，
是你用來延後自己的說法。
不用等到全部清空，
挑一件最小的，今天就先做。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種永遠把自己排最後一位的朋友，或是自己看。重點在最後一句：不是要你全部處理完，是先做一件就好。
variations: 「這陣子」不會結束，它只會換一批事情繼續叫這個名字。
先做那件最小的：預約、回訊息、喝完那杯水。

en.content: You keep filing things under "once I get through this busy stretch." The coffee you meant to schedule, the doctor you meant to see, the call you meant to return. But that stretch has been running for years now. It isn't a date that arrives — it's the phrase you use to postpone yourself. You don't have to clear the whole list. Pick the smallest one and do it today.
en.editorNote: For the friend who always puts themselves last, or for you. The point is the last line: not finish everything, just one thing.
variations: "This busy stretch" never ends. It just hands the name to the next pile.
Start with the smallest one: book it, reply to it, drink the glass of water.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 zh-tw counseling writing on needing time to process endings; cinema-credits scene written original

zh-tw.content:
電影演完，燈亮了，旁邊的人開始穿外套。
你還坐著，看字幕一行一行往上跑。
那不是你反應慢，
是有些東西需要一段安靜，才會真的落地。
剛結束的那件事——
那段關係、那份工作、那場考試——
也有它自己的字幕時間。
還沒站起來，不代表你走不出去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛結束一段關係或一份工作、身邊的人已經開始問「你還好嗎、怎麼還沒振作」的時候。
variations: 散場的燈亮了，不代表你也得同時結束。
結束需要時間跑完，就像片尾一樣。

en.content: The movie ends, the lights come up, and everyone around you starts reaching for their jackets. You're still sitting there, watching the credits scroll. That isn't slowness. Some things need a stretch of quiet before they actually land. The thing that just ended — the relationship, the job, the exam — has its own credit roll. Still in your seat doesn't mean you're stuck.
en.editorNote: For right after a breakup or a job ending, when people have already started asking why you haven't bounced back yet.
variations: The house lights coming on doesn't mean you're done too.
Endings take time to finish rolling. Let yours.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 zh-tw material on how stress shows up in the body before it reaches words; rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
洗手的時候刺了一下，
你才發現指甲旁邊那塊皮又被自己撕掉了。
什麼時候撕的，你完全沒印象。
開會的時候、等回覆的時候、聽到某個名字的時候——
嘴巴說沒事，手指先招了。
身體不太會演戲，
它只是先幫你把緊張放在一個地方。
下次痛的時候別罵自己，
那是它在告訴你：這件事你其實很在意。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「明明沒發生什麼事，卻一直很緊繃」的日子。把身體的小動作當成訊息讀，而不是壞習慣。
variations: 你的手比你誠實，它早就知道你在緊張。
身體先說出口的事，通常是你還不敢承認在意的事。

en.content: You feel the sting under the tap and realize you've picked the skin beside your nail raw again. You have no memory of doing it. In the meeting, waiting on a reply, hearing a certain name — your mouth says you're fine, and your hands give you away first. The body isn't a good actor. It just parks the tension somewhere for you. Next time it stings, don't scold yourself. It's telling you this one actually matters to you.
en.editorNote: For those days when nothing has happened and you're still wound tight. Read the small physical habits as information, not as a flaw.
variations: Your hands are more honest than you are. They knew first.
What the body says out loud is usually what you haven't admitted you care about.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Taiwan's August 2026 afternoon-thunderstorm season as an emotional metaphor; fully rewritten original

zh-tw.content:
下午三點的雨大到看不見對面的招牌，
你站在騎樓底下，覺得今天大概哪裡都去不成了。
二十分鐘後太陽出來，地上只剩幾攤水在反光。
最壞的那一段心情也是這種下法，
又急又滿，讓人以為會一直這樣下去。
所以先不要在雨最大的時候，決定你的一整天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合情緒突然湧上來、覺得整個人被淹掉的那個下午。不是叫你別難過，是提醒你別在最強的那一刻替一整天下判斷。
variations: 雨最大的那十分鐘，不適合用來決定任何事。
等地上開始反光的時候，你再看一次今天。

en.content: At three in the afternoon the rain comes down so hard you can't read the sign across the street, and you stand under the arcade deciding the whole day is a write-off. Twenty minutes later the sun is back and all that's left are a few puddles catching the light. The worst stretch of a mood arrives the same way — fast, total, convincing you it will stay. So don't decide how your day is going while the rain is still at its loudest.
en.editorNote: For the afternoon when a feeling swamps you out of nowhere. Not a reason to stop feeling it, just a reason not to sentence the whole day mid-downpour.
variations: The loudest ten minutes of the storm are the worst time to decide anything.
Wait until the puddles start catching light, then look at today again.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by zh-tw discussion of adjustment periods after life changes; rewritten as an original phone-update scene

zh-tw.content:
手機半夜自己更新完，早上打開，
連相機在哪裡你都要找一下。
那幾天你按錯好幾次，心裡有點煩，開始懷疑自己是不是退步了。
可是東西都還在，只是位置換了，手指需要一點時間重新記住。
換部門、搬家、身邊的人變了之後，
你現在的笨拙也是同一種笨拙。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛換環境、覺得自己做什麼都卡卡的人。把「不熟悉」和「變差」分開來看，就會沒那麼焦躁。
variations: 你沒有變慢，你只是還在找每個按鈕的新位置。
剛換環境的那幾週，本來就會一直按錯。

en.content: Your phone updated itself overnight, and now you have to hunt for the camera icon. For a few days you keep tapping the wrong thing, getting annoyed, wondering if you're losing your edge. But nothing is gone — it just moved, and your thumbs need time to relearn where. New team, new apartment, a changed circle of people: the clumsiness you're feeling now is exactly that kind of clumsiness.
en.editorNote: For anyone in a fresh environment who feels like they've suddenly gotten worse at everything. Separating 'unfamiliar' from 'declining' takes a lot of pressure off.
variations: You haven't slowed down. You're still learning where the buttons moved to.
The first few weeks anywhere new, tapping the wrong thing is standard.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by material on non-verbal companionship and quiet presence; rewritten as an original scene

zh-tw.content:
你坐在地板上發呆，貓走過來，
沒有叫，也沒有蹭，就在你旁邊躺下。
牠不會問你為什麼心情不好，也不會叫你想開一點。
手摸到牠背上溫溫的那一下，
你才發現自己剛剛一直閉著氣。
有些陪伴不需要聽懂你，只需要肯待在同一個房間。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合說不出口、也不想被追問的那種難受。傳給那個總是安靜待在你旁邊的人，或在自己需要被安靜陪著的時候讀。
variations: 不問為什麼的陪伴，有時候比任何建議都有用。
有人願意待在同一個房間裡，你就已經沒那麼撐著了。

en.content: You're sitting on the floor staring at nothing when the cat walks over, doesn't meow, doesn't rub against you, just lies down beside you. She won't ask why you're upset or tell you to look on the bright side. The moment your hand finds the warm spot on her back, you notice you've been holding your breath. Some company doesn't need to understand you — it just needs to stay in the room.
en.editorNote: For the kind of low you can't explain and don't want questioned. Send it to whoever quietly sits with you, or read it when that's what you need.
variations: Company that doesn't ask why can beat any advice.
Someone willing to stay in the room takes half the weight off already.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by zh-tw writing on small anticipations as a coping resource; rewritten as an original parcel-tracking scene

zh-tw.content:
你買了一個很小的東西給自己，三天內已經點開物流頁面四次。
上面永遠寫著配送中，你看完就關掉，過兩個小時又點開。
講出來有點好笑，你這幾天唯一在期待的事情就只有這個。
但願意替明天留下一格期待的人，
正在用自己的方法把自己撐住。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合日子很平、也沒什麼盼頭的那一週。小小的期待不需要很有意義，它的功能是讓明天有個形狀。
variations: 為明天留一件小事可以期待，這件事本身就有用。
很小的期待也算期待，它一樣能把你帶到下禮拜。

en.content: You bought yourself something small and you've opened the tracking page four times in three days. It always says out for delivery; you close it and open it again two hours later. It sounds a little ridiculous, that this is the only thing you've looked forward to all week. But somebody who keeps one slot of anticipation open for tomorrow is holding themselves together in their own way.
en.editorNote: For a flat week with nothing on the horizon. A small thing to look forward to doesn't need to be meaningful — its job is to give tomorrow a shape.
variations: Leaving one small thing to look forward to is doing real work.
A tiny bit of anticipation still counts, and it still carries you to next week.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 Taiwan workplace-burnout coverage on unspoken needs at work; rewritten as an original office scene

zh-tw.content:
同事問你會不會冷的時候，你笑一笑說還好。
其實你桌子底下放著一件薄外套，
八月天在辦公室穿了整整一個月。
辦公室的溫度通常是最早開口的那個人決定的，而你每次都讓別人先講。
把「我有點冷」說出口，不會讓你變成一個很難相處的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「講出來好像很麻煩」而一路忍下去的人。從最小、最無害的需求開始練習開口，比一次要求大事容易得多。
variations: 先講的人不是比較自私，只是比較敢麻煩別人一次。
從一句「我有點冷」開始練，比較不會嚇到自己。

en.content: When a coworker asks if you're cold, you smile and say you're fine. Meanwhile there's a thin jacket under your desk that you've worn all month, in August. Office temperature usually gets set by whoever speaks up first, and you always let that be someone else. Saying 'I'm a little cold' out loud is not going to turn you into a difficult person.
en.editorNote: For anyone who swallows small requests because raising them feels like a hassle. Practicing on the smallest, most harmless need is far easier than starting with a big ask.
variations: The person who speaks up first isn't selfish. They're just willing to inconvenience someone once.
Start with 'I'm a little cold.' It's the least scary place to practice.

items.sourceNote: 台灣職場過勞指數報導提到長期緊繃被當成常態；改寫成一段推拿檯上的原創對白

zh-tw.content:
「這裡按會痛嗎？」
「還好。」
「這一整塊都硬掉了，摸起來像板子，你這樣扛著走多久了？」
你趴在那裡沒回話，因為你真的算不出來，只記得從某一年開始，肩膀緊、脖子卡就被你歸進日常，不再算是一件需要處理的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 寫給那種把長期緊繃當成體質、被外人按到才想起來的人。
variations: 身體不會突然硬掉，它是一天一點被你借去撐場面的。
被別人說「這裡很硬」的時候，先別急著說還好。

en.content: "Does it hurt when I press here?" "Not really." "This whole area is locked up like a board, so how long have you been carrying it around?" You lay there without answering, because you honestly couldn't count, and somewhere along the way a tight shoulder stopped registering as a problem and just became part of the furniture.
en.editorNote: For anyone who has quietly reclassified chronic tension as their personality until a stranger's thumb says otherwise.
variations: Nothing seizes up overnight. You lent it out one day at a time.
When someone says 'this is really tight,' try not to answer with 'not really.'

items.sourceNote: 停止精神內耗的文章談到把別人的行為讀成針對自己；改寫成一則原創的鄰居誤會場景

zh-tw.content:
樓上那戶每天過了十二點還在走來走去，你在床上翻身，心裡唸過好幾次。
有天早上在電梯遇到，他手上提著還沒吃的便當，制服皺得很厲害。
你才知道他每天回到家的時間，就是你被吵醒的那個時間。
同一段聲音，你聽了半年才聽懂它在說什麼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合最近很容易把別人的動靜讀成惡意的人，多數噪音底下都有一個也在撐的人。
variations: 你聽見的吵，有時候是別人一天的結尾。
在生氣之前多知道一件事，氣就會少掉一大半。

en.content: The unit upstairs is still pacing around well past midnight, and you have grumbled at the ceiling more times than you can count. One morning you run into the guy in the elevator, holding a lunch box he hasn't opened, uniform completely wrinkled. That's when it lands that the hour you keep getting woken up is the hour he finally gets home. Same footsteps for half a year, and you only just heard what they were saying.
en.editorNote: For anyone currently reading every small disturbance as something aimed at them.
variations: The noise that wakes you up is sometimes the end of somebody else's day.
One extra fact about a person takes most of the anger out of the room.

items.sourceNote: 療癒專題提到「看起來沒用的準備其實在提供安全感」；改寫成一支雨傘的第一人稱獨白

zh-tw.content:
我在你包包最底層躺了兩個禮拜，一次都沒被撐開過。
每天出門前你都會看一眼天氣，然後還是把我塞進去。
帶著我的那些日子多半沒下雨，你大概覺得自己白帶了一趟又一趟。
可是你這兩個禮拜都乾乾地走完全程，那就是我在做的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 獻給那些做了很多沒被用到的準備、因此覺得自己白忙的人。
variations: 沒派上用場的準備，換來的是你一路上不用擔心。
有些東西的功勞，是那件事根本沒發生。

en.content: I've been lying at the bottom of your bag for two weeks and you haven't opened me once. Every morning you check the forecast and shove me in anyway. Most of those days stayed dry, so you probably figured you hauled me around for nothing. But you walked every one of those blocks without once worrying about it, and that was the whole job.
en.editorNote: For anyone who feels silly about all the preparation that never got used.
variations: Preparation that goes unused buys you a walk with nothing on your mind.
Some things earn their keep by making sure nothing happens.

items.sourceNote: 情緒調節文章提到「對方的喜怒是他的課題」；改寫成三段條件句的原創練習

zh-tw.content:
如果有人語氣突然變硬，你先在心裡數三秒再接話。
如果三秒過了你還是很想先道歉，就問自己一句：這件事真的是我做的嗎？
如果答案是不確定，你可以什麼都不承認，先把話停在那裡。
別人的口氣是他自己那一天的事，不用每次都算到你頭上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一被兇就自動反射道歉、事後才發現根本不關自己的事的人。
variations: 那三秒不用拿來想怎麼回話，拿來確認自己站在哪裡就好。
先確認是不是你的事，再決定要不要道歉。

en.content: If someone's tone goes sharp, count three seconds in your head before you answer. If you still want to apologize after those three seconds, ask yourself whether this thing is actually yours to apologize for. If the answer is anything short of yes, you're allowed to admit nothing and just let the sentence sit there. Somebody's tone belongs to their day, and it doesn't have to get charged to your account.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose reflex is to apologize the second a voice hardens, only to realize later it was never theirs.
variations: Those three seconds aren't avoidance. They're the part that belongs to you.
Check whose problem it is first, then decide about the apology.

items.sourceNote: 文章談內耗多半來自對未來的災難化預演；改寫成自問自答結構的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
你問自己這陣子到底累在哪裡，翻開行事曆卻沒幾件大事。
真正把電吃光的，是你每天在腦子裡先演一遍那些還沒發生的壞結果。
一場沒有觀眾的排練，你卻認真到滿身大汗。
今天可以缺席一次，那個劇本從來也沒照演過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合明明沒做什麼卻累到不行、後來才發現自己整天都在腦中演最壞版本的人。
variations: 行事曆很空的那一週，你可能累在還沒發生的事情上。
把預演的力氣留著，等事情真的發生再拿出來用。

en.content: You ask yourself why you're this wiped out, then open your calendar and find almost nothing on it. The thing draining you is the daily habit of running tomorrow's worst version in your head before it happens. That's a full dress rehearsal with no audience, and you keep showing up soaked in sweat. You're allowed to skip one, because the script never gets performed the way you wrote it.
en.editorNote: For anyone exhausted by a light week they spent rehearsing worst cases.
variations: A light week can still wipe you out if you spend it rehearsing disasters.
Save the energy for the version that actually shows up.

items.sourceNote: 文章談「我好累」是情緒超載的訊號而非懶惰；改寫成司機旁觀視角的原創短文

zh-tw.content:
半夜載到一個客人，報完地址就沒再開口。
車開到一半，後照鏡裡看到他終於把肩膀放下來，整個人往椅背陷進去。
到了樓下他坐著沒動，我也沒催，等他自己深呼吸完才開門。
那十幾分鐘的車程，大概是他一整天唯一沒有人等他回應的時間。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合整天都在應付別人、需要一段沒人要你回話的空白時間的人。
variations: 終於沒有人在等你回答的那段路，也算是休息。
有人願意讓你安靜坐完全程，那是一種溫柔。

en.content: Picked up a guy after midnight who gave me the address and then went quiet. Halfway there I caught him in the mirror letting his shoulders drop, sinking back into the seat like he'd been holding them up since morning. We got to his building and he didn't move, so I didn't rush him, just waited out the long breath before I popped the door. Those fifteen minutes were probably the only stretch of his whole day when nobody was waiting on him to answer.
en.editorNote: For anyone who spends all day responding to people and needs a window where nobody needs an answer.
variations: A ride where nobody needs you to answer still counts as rest.
Letting someone sit in silence is its own kind of kindness.

items.sourceNote: 心理師談忙碌者的自我對話練習；改寫成為日常詞下非字典定義的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
下次你手機震動的時候，大概會是禮拜六下午三點，對方問你有沒有空。

拇指會比你快，答應的話幾乎是自己跑出來的。

在送出之前先停三秒，低頭看一下自己的肩膀有沒有垮下來。

垮下來的話，就把訊息改成：這個週末我想留給自己，下週再約好嗎。

打完直接送出，不要重讀，也不要補一句對不起。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個週末行事曆空著、卻從來沒真的休息到的朋友
variations: 拇指會比你快，答應的話幾乎是自己跑出來的。
送出之前先停三秒，看一下自己的肩膀有沒有垮下來。

en.content:
Next time your phone buzzes it'll be around three on a Saturday, and somebody will be asking if you're free.

Your thumb moves faster than you do. The yes practically types itself.

Give it three seconds before you hit send, and look down at your shoulders to see whether they've dropped.

If they have, change the message to this: I'm keeping this weekend for myself, can we do next week instead?

Send it exactly like that. Don't reread it, and don't tack on an apology.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend whose weekends look wide open and somehow never turn into rest
variations: Your thumb moves faster than you do, and the yes types itself.
Three seconds before you send: check whether your shoulders have dropped.

items.sourceNote: 心理師談情緒耗竭的恢復是漸進而無聲的；改寫成指涉未來場景的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
會有那麼一個很普通的下午，你站在超市貨架前挑東西，突然想不起來上一次胸口發悶是什麼時候。
沒有人會通知你，收銀機還是一樣嗶嗶地響。
你提著袋子走回家，等紅燈的時候想起這件事，自己笑了一下。
那天還沒到，可是它已經在往你這邊移動了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合正在低谷、覺得這種狀態永遠不會結束的人。
variations: 低潮結束的時候通常沒有聲音，你會晚一點才發現。
那天不會敲鑼打鼓，它會在很普通的地方等你。

en.content: There's an ordinary afternoon coming where you'll be standing in a grocery aisle and realize you can't remember the last time your chest went tight. Nobody announces it and the register keeps beeping like always. You'll carry the bags home, remember it at a red light, and catch yourself smiling. That day hasn't shown up yet, but it's already moving toward you.
en.editorNote: For anyone in the low part who can't picture it ending.
variations: The low part usually ends quietly, and you notice it late.
That day won't announce itself. It'll just be a very ordinary afternoon.

items.sourceNote: 自我疼惜文章談「一次只做一件小事」的復原方式；改寫成停車場繳費機的時刻表原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
21:47　把車停好，沒有熄火，把最後一首歌聽完。
21:53　走到繳費機前面，皮夾裡只有一張皺掉的百元鈔。
21:55　機器退了三次，第四次終於嗶了一聲。
21:56　找零掉下來，聲音大到整層樓都聽得到。
22:01　我把那幾個銅板握在手裡，走回車上一直搓。
22:04　柵欄慢慢抬起來，像有人替我點了個頭。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合下班太晚、一整天沒被誰好好對待的日子。
variations: 有些日子撐過去的證據，只是一張皺掉的鈔票終於被機器收下。
沒有人替你鼓掌的時候，柵欄抬起來也算數。

en.content:
9:47pm — Parked, engine still running, finished the last song.
9:53pm — Walked to the payment machine with one crumpled bill in my wallet.
9:55pm — It spat the bill back three times, then finally beeped.
9:56pm — The change dropped so loud the whole level heard it.
10:01pm — Held the coins in my fist the whole way back to the car.
10:04pm — The gate lifted slowly, like somebody nodding at me.
en.editorNote: For nights you got home late and nobody was gentle with you all day.
variations: Some days the proof you made it is a crumpled bill the machine finally accepts.
When nobody claps for you, a gate lifting counts.

items.sourceNote: 心理師談耗竭時最缺的是對自己的寬容；改寫成深夜自助加油站的表單體原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
車輛狀況：後座還躺著上禮拜的收據，我一直沒清。
油品種類：九五，跟上次一樣，今天沒力氣做新的決定。
加油金額：五百就好，剩下的路明天再說。
目前狀態：站在油槍旁邊發呆，聞到味道才想起自己還沒吃飯。
是否需要協助：需要。但這一欄我還是會勾「否」。
備註：今天沒有搞砸什麼，這樣就算過關。
簽名：字有點歪，反正只有我自己會看。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一個人開夜車、什麼都還撐得住但很想被問一句的時候。
variations: 有些晚上只加得動五百塊的油，那也夠開到明天。
有些欄位我會誠實填，只是不會交出去。

en.content:
Vehicle condition: Last week's receipts still on the back seat. Never cleared them.
Fuel type: Same as last time. No energy for new decisions today.
Amount: Just enough for tonight. The rest of the road can wait.
Current state: Standing by the pump, realizing from the smell that I haven't eaten.
Need assistance: Yes. But I'll still tick "no" on this line.
Notes: Didn't ruin anything today. That counts as a pass.
Signature: A little crooked. Nobody reads it but me.
en.editorNote: For the solo night drive when you're holding up fine and wish someone would ask anyway.
variations: Some nights you can only afford half a tank, and half a tank gets you to tomorrow.
Some forms I fill out honestly and never hand in.

items.sourceNote: 療癒語錄合輯談復原發生在日常的小片刻；改寫成一個人吃火鍋的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
一個人吃火鍋，湯滾起來的時候我把肉片一片一片鋪進去，在心裡數秒。
手機震了一下，是明天開會的提醒，我按掉，順手把三個醬料碟排成一直線。
豆皮浮上來的那一刻，霧氣把我的眼鏡糊成一片白。
我沒有擦，就這樣坐了一會兒，心裡想的是——這一鍋沒有人在旁邊等我，我可以吃得很慢很慢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛學會一個人吃飯、還在習慣安靜的人。
variations: 一個人的鍋不用配合誰的速度，這件事我很晚才學會。
眼鏡糊掉的那幾秒，是我一整天最不用交代什麼的時候。

en.content: Eating hot pot alone, laying the slices in one at a time, counting seconds in my head. My phone buzzes with a reminder about tomorrow's meeting, so I dismiss it and line up the three sauce dishes in a row. When the tofu skin floats up, the steam fogs my glasses completely white. I don't wipe them. I just sit there a while, thinking: nobody is waiting on this pot, so I can eat as slowly as I want.
en.editorNote: For anyone still getting used to eating alone.
variations: A pot for one doesn't have to match anyone's pace. Took me years to learn that.
Those few foggy seconds were the only part of the day I owed no one an explanation.

items.sourceNote: 文章談剪髮作為情緒調節與身分轉換的象徵；改寫成兩個時期、兩間理髮店的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
十九歲那年在學校側門那間店，我盯著鏡子說「短一點沒關係」，心裡想的是把某個人從頭上剪掉。
上個月換到公司樓下這間，一樣的鏡子，一樣的那句話，我說完就低頭滑手機了。
差別在於這次剪完，我沒有急著確認自己好不好看。
圍布拆下來的時候脖子涼涼的，這一次掉在地上的就真的只有頭髮。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合走過一段感情、發現自己已經不痛的時候。
variations: 同一句話說第二次的時候，重量已經不一樣了。
有些告別不用宣布，你只會在鏡子前面發現它結束了。

en.content: At nineteen, in the shop by the campus side gate, I stared at the mirror and said "short is fine" — meaning I wanted to cut someone off my head. Last month, at the shop under my office, same mirror, same sentence, and I went straight back to my phone after saying it. The difference is that this time I wasn't in a rush to check whether I looked okay. When the cape came off and my neck went cool, the only thing on the floor was hair.
en.editorNote: For the moment you realize an old heartbreak has stopped hurting.
variations: The second time you say the same line, it weighs a different amount.
Some goodbyes don't get announced. You just notice them in a mirror.

items.sourceNote: 台視報導修鞋師傅承襲父業、半世紀惜鞋惜情；改寫成修鞋攤問答體的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
修鞋攤的三個常見問題（回答的人手上都是黑的）
1. 這雙還能修嗎？
能。縫線會留一道痕，走近看得出來。
2. 可以修到跟新的一樣嗎？
修不到。它以後會有自己的穿法，跟新鞋各走各的路。
3. 要等多久？
放我這裡三天。今天就要穿走的話我先上膠，那撐不過一場雨。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合復原到一半、還在意自己身上留下痕跡的時候。
variations: 修好的東西都看得出縫過的地方，那是它被留下來的證據。
趕時間的補救只撐得住晴天。

en.content:
Three questions people ask at the shoe repair stall (the guy answering has black hands)
1. Can this pair still be saved?
Yes. The new stitching leaves a line you can see up close.
2. Can you make them like new?
No. They'll walk their own way from here, and new shoes walk theirs.
3. How long does it take?
Leave them three days. If you need them on your feet tonight I'll just glue it, and glue won't survive one rain.
en.editorNote: For when you're half-healed and still self-conscious about the seam it left.
variations: Anything repaired shows the stitch. That's the proof it got kept.
A rushed fix only holds in good weather.

items.sourceNote: 北市圖說明逾期還書計費與三日緩衝期；改寫成還書櫃台問答體的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
還書櫃台的三個常見問題（櫃台後面那位不會抬頭看你）
1. 逾期很久了，會不會很麻煩？
不會。前三天本來就有緩衝，你在心裡多罵自己的那幾天，系統沒有在算。
2. 要不要先解釋一下原因？
不用。書放上去就好，這裡沒有人問過為什麼。
3. 之後還可以再借嗎？
可以。還完就算清了，下一本照樣讓你帶走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合把一件小事拖到不敢面對、光想到就先自責的時候。
variations: 拖著的那幾天，利息只有你自己在付。
有些事情你只要放回去，它就結束了。

en.content:
Three questions people ask at the returns desk (the person behind it won't look up at you)
1. It's very overdue. Am I in trouble?
No. The first few days are a grace period anyway, and the extra days you spent scolding yourself were never counted.
2. Should I explain why I kept it so long?
No need. Just set it down. Nobody here has ever asked why.
3. Can I still borrow something today?
Yes. Once it's back, it's settled, and the next one goes home with you like always.
en.editorNote: For when a small task got put off so long that facing it feels worse than it is.
variations: All those days of putting it off, you were the only one paying interest.
Some things end the moment you hand them back.

items.sourceNote: 節氣專欄談 8/23 處暑後晝熱夜涼、夜間蓋薄被護腰腹；改寫成白天撐住、晚上垮掉的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
處暑之後開始晝熱夜涼，白天照樣曬到冒汗，太陽一下山溫度就掉五六度。
你的一天大概也是這樣，白天在會議裡講話很正常，回到家坐在床邊卻沒力氣脫襪子。
別人只看得到白天那一段，所以你常常覺得自己好像在裝沒事。
兩個溫度都是真的，中間差的那幾度，本來就該有人替你蓋一件薄的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合白天撐得住、一回到家就整個垮下來的人。
variations: 白天的你跟晚上的你是同一個人，只是溫度不一樣。
回家以後掉下來的那幾度，不用跟誰報備。

en.content: After the summer heat officially breaks, the days still cook you and the temperature falls five or six degrees the moment the sun goes down. Your own day probably runs the same way: you speak fine in meetings, then sit on the edge of the bed at home with no energy left to pull your socks off. People only ever see the daytime half, so you keep suspecting you're faking something. Both temperatures are real, and the gap between them is exactly where somebody should be handing you a thin blanket.
en.editorNote: For anyone who holds it together all day and collapses the second they get home.
variations: Daytime you and night-time you are the same person at two temperatures.
The degrees you drop after getting home don't have to be reported to anyone.

items.sourceNote: 媽媽寶寶整理 2026 學年 8/31 開學行事曆與開學前收心；改寫成文具店裡的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
「還要買一樣的？舊的那本明明還能用。」
開學前一個禮拜，你在文具店站了很久，最後還是拿了同一款筆記本。
你知道自己沒那麼需要它，可是握在手上的時候，肩膀確實鬆了一點。
用一本新的簿子替自己重開一局，這種小儀式沒有規定要成熟到不需要。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開學、換季或任何你想從頭來過的節點。
variations: 重新開始不用等大事發生，一本空白的簿子就夠了。
有些安慰很便宜，可是它對你真的有效。

en.content:
"Another one exactly like it? The old notebook still works fine."
A week before school starts, you stand in the stationery aisle for a long time and walk out with the same notebook you always buy. You know you don't really need it, but holding it, your shoulders drop half an inch. Opening a blank one to restart the round is a small ritual, and nobody ever ruled that grown-ups have to outgrow it.
en.editorNote: For the start of a school year, a season, or any point you want to begin again.
variations: A fresh start doesn't wait for something big. A blank notebook covers it.
Some comfort is cheap and still works on you.

items.sourceNote: ETtoday 2026/07 報導資深新秘指出「新娘休息室」名不符實、新娘全程趕場沒空喝水；改寫成婚宴散場後往回推的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
散場之後，你終於在婚宴會場的休息室裡坐下來，鞋子脫掉，把那杯早就退冰的水一口喝完。
往前推兩個小時，你在同一張椅子上換第三套禮服，親戚推門進來借插座，你笑著說沒關係。
再往前推一個早上，你在這裡補了四次妝，桌上那份給你的早餐一口也沒動過。
再往前，是半年前你點頭說「好啊，那就辦」的那個晚上，你腦中浮現的畫面是所有人笑著舉杯。
那天晚上的你，其實也把自己算在那些人裡面。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛忙完一場大場面的人，或那種為了讓大家開心、忙到忘記自己也在場的朋友。
variations: 一場為了讓大家開心的場合，你也在那個「大家」裡面。
今天結束前，記得替自己留一杯不用敬給誰的水。

en.content:
After the last guest leaves, you finally sit down in the reception hall's back room, kick off the shoes, and drink the whole glass of water that went warm hours ago.
Rewind two hours: same chair, third dress change, a relative pushing the door open to borrow the outlet, and you smiling that it's fine.
Rewind one more morning: four touch-ups at this same table, and the breakfast someone set out for you still untouched.
Rewind further, to the night six months ago when you nodded and said okay, let's do it, picturing a room full of people laughing with their glasses up.
That version of you was counting herself among those people too.
en.editorNote: For anyone who just pulled off a big event, or the friend who ran the whole day for everyone else and forgot they were there too.
variations: If the day was meant to make everyone happy, you are part of everyone.
Before today ends, pour one glass you don't have to raise to anybody.

items.sourceNote: 自我疼惜相關整理指出自我批評常內化成日常反應、且善待自己是可練習的技能；改寫成剪髮椅前那面鏡子的獨白

zh-tw.content:
我是這間店裡最舊的一面鏡子，一天大概要照過三十幾個人。
坐上這張椅子的人幾乎都會先做同一件事：下巴往內收，肩膀往裡縮，好像先替自己的臉道個歉。
剪到一半他們就忘了，開始講小孩、講工作、講上禮拜那件很煩的事，身體一寸一寸攤回去。
那個攤回去的樣子，在我看來才比較接近本人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個照相前總要先擋一下臉、覺得自己怎麼樣都不夠好看的人。
variations: 你坐下來時縮起來的那些地方，其實沒有人要求你縮。
講到自己在乎的事情時，你的樣子最好看，可惜你當下都沒在看。

en.content:
I'm the oldest mirror in this shop, and about thirty faces pass through me a day.
Almost everyone who sits in that chair does the same thing first: chin tucked in, shoulders pulled small, like apologizing to their own face before anyone speaks.
Halfway through the cut they forget, and start talking about their kid, their job, that annoying thing from last week, and the body unfolds an inch at a time.
The unfolded version is the one I'd say looks the most like them.
en.editorNote: Send it to the person who always blocks their face before a photo and thinks they never look right.
variations: Nobody asked you to make yourself smaller in the chair.
You look best while talking about something you care about, which is exactly when you're not looking.

items.sourceNote: Scientific Reports 研究指出自我疼惜與人際共通感在復原歷程中的保護作用、且復原需要時間累積；改寫成火鍋店鍋邊的原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
這一頓你推掉過五次，第六次答應的時候，訊息打了又刪，前後花掉十一分鐘。
店裡的鍋從冷水到滾要八分鐘，那八分鐘你們什麼正事都沒講，只認真討論了醬料要不要加蔥。
整頓飯坐了兩小時十分鐘，你真正想說的那句話，是在最後二十分鐘才掉出來的。
對方聽完沒有給你任何建議，只是又幫你撈了一次快要煮爛的高麗菜。
有些話得先泡在熱氣裡兩個小時才出得了喉嚨，這個時間成本很合理。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合約人吃飯卻不知道怎麼開口的時候，也適合傳給那個一直說「改天啦」的朋友。
variations: 有些話需要一鍋湯的時間才煮得開，別急著在第一分鐘逼自己講完。
陪你坐滿兩個小時的人，通常比急著給你建議的人有用。

en.content:
You canceled this dinner five times, and when you finally said yes on the sixth, you typed and deleted for eleven minutes straight.
The pot takes eight minutes to go from cold water to a boil, and in those eight minutes you two covered nothing important, only whether the sauce needed scallions.
The meal ran two hours and ten minutes, and the sentence you actually came to say fell out somewhere in the last twenty.
They didn't hand you a single piece of advice, just fished the overcooked cabbage out of the broth for you again.
Some sentences need two hours of steam before the throat will release them, and that's a fair price.
en.editorNote: For when you want to talk but can't start, or for the friend who keeps saying "some other time."
variations: Some things need a whole pot's worth of time to soften. Don't force them out in minute one.
The person who sits there for two hours usually helps more than the one with advice ready.

items.sourceNote: Heho 健康引述 PLOS One 研究指出造訪河流環境與心理健康正相關、比其他環境更有療癒與安全感；改寫成河堤步道上的兩人對話

zh-tw.content:
「你今天走這麼慢，是不是哪裡不舒服？」
「沒有，我只是想把這段河堤走久一點。」
「那我們走到橋下就折返，還是要走到對岸那排燈亮起來的地方？」
「都可以啊，反正走多遠你都在旁邊。」
「那就這樣走吧，風又沒有在趕我們。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個會配合你步速的人，或是你們散步完各自回家的那個晚上。
variations: 有人願意配合你的步速，這件事比任何一句鼓勵都實在。
「我陪你走到那裡就好」，這種句子可以撐很多天。

en.content:
"You're walking really slowly today. Something wrong?"
"No, I just want this stretch of the riverbank to last longer."
"Then do we turn around at the bridge, or keep going till those lights across the water come on?"
"Either way. However far it is, you're next to me."
"Let's just keep going then. The wind isn't rushing us."
en.editorNote: For the person who matches your pace, or for the night after a walk when you both head home.
variations: Someone willing to match your pace beats any pep talk.
"I'll walk with you that far" is a sentence that holds up for days.

items.sourceNote: 人間福報〈市場的人情味〉描寫傳統市場攤商與客人之間不必多說的照顧；改寫成一則先講結論再回頭交代原因的自述

zh-tw.content:
我現在比較敢承認自己不會。
那天我捧著一把叫不出名字的野菜，在攤子邊站了好一陣子。
阿姨伸手把菜抽走，說這個得先燙過再炒，回去照做就對了。
她沒有笑我，也沒有多問一句，只是把該講的講完。
把「我不會」說出口的那一刻，事情就鬆掉了一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個總是硬撐、寧可自己亂猜也不肯開口問人的人。
variations: 承認自己不會，比裝懂省下更多力氣。
願意直接教你的人，通常也懶得記住你笨過的那一秒。

en.content:
I'm a lot better now at admitting I don't know how.
That morning I stood by the stall for ages, holding a bunch of greens I couldn't name.
The woman running it pulled them out of my hand and told me to blanch them first, then stir-fry, and just do it that way at home.
She didn't laugh at me or ask anything else. She said what needed saying and went back to work.
The second "I don't know how" left my mouth, the whole thing got lighter.
en.editorNote: For the person who would rather guess badly forever than ask a single question.
variations: Admitting you don't know costs less than pretending you do.
People willing to just show you rarely bother remembering you didn't know.

items.sourceNote: 照護線上談看牙恐懼與焦慮，提到失去控制感、器械聲響與未知感是主要來源；改寫成一段自問自答的內心對話

zh-tw.content:
到底在怕什麼，我問過自己好幾次。
是那個機器的聲音嗎？想想又不太像，麻藥上了以後也幾乎沒感覺，真正難熬的反而是它突然停下來的空檔。
拖了好久我才願意承認，我怕的是那幾分鐘只能躺著、張著嘴，一句話都說不了。
但那幾分鐘每次都會結束，而且每一次我都自己撐完了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在做完一件你其實很怕的例行小事之後，寫給自己看。
variations: 有些害怕拆開來看，剩下的其實只是「不能喊停」這件事。
撐完一次，下一次就有一個可以拿出來用的證據。

en.content:
What was I actually afraid of? I put that question to myself more than once.
The sound of the drill? Not quite, and the pain barely registers once the numbing sets in — the harder part is the gap when it suddenly stops.
It took me a long time to admit that what scares me is those few minutes of lying there with my mouth open, unable to say a single word.
But those minutes always end, and so far I've gotten through every one of them on my own.
en.editorNote: For after you've finished some small routine thing that quietly terrifies you.
variations: Take a fear apart and what's often left is just "I can't call time out."
Getting through it once gives you something to hold up next time.

items.sourceNote: PopDaily 盤點校園經典回憶，提到社課留下來團練、學長姊傳承等場景；改寫成對已畢業學姊說話的第二人稱短文

zh-tw.content:
學姊，我們社課那間教室的燈管還是會閃。
我現在坐的就是你以前那張椅子，椅背照樣會慢慢往後滑。
你畢業前跟我說，帶不動大家就先讓他們笑一下，我到現在還在用這招。
這句話你大概早就忘了，我卻靠它撐過了三年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給一個已經離開、你也沒機會好好道謝的人。
variations: 有些人隨口留下的一句話，會在你身上待得比他們久。
你不用讓他知道，那句話已經替你擋掉很多次了。

en.content:
The light in our club room still flickers, you know.
I sit in the chair you used to take, and the back still slides down slowly, same as always.
Before you graduated you told me that when I can't get the room moving, make them laugh first. I still use that.
You've probably forgotten you ever said it. I've been living on it for three years.
en.editorNote: For someone who left before you got the chance to thank them properly.
variations: Something a person says offhand can outlast them in you.
They never have to know how many times that line held you up.

items.sourceNote: 農傳媒報導舊衣修改店，提到修改是讓衣服回頭配合穿的人；改寫成十七歲與三十歲兩個時間點的對照

zh-tw.content:
十七歲的我把制服裙頭往內摺了兩摺，只想跟大家長得一樣。
三十歲的我站在改衣服的小店裡，跟師傅說腰放寬一點，袖子留長也沒關係。
以前在意的是有沒有被看見，現在在意的是待不待得住。
師傅低頭畫著粉線，說衣服本來就得配合人，不然改它做什麼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你終於買了一件「舒服但不夠亮眼」的衣服那天。
variations: 願意讓衣服配合自己，也是一種長大。
合身的定義會變，那代表你也變了。

en.content:
At seventeen I rolled my uniform skirt twice at the waist, just to look like everyone else.
At thirty I'm standing in a little alteration shop asking for the waist let out and the sleeves left long.
Back then I cared about being seen. Now I care about being able to stay.
The tailor kept drawing her chalk line and said clothes are supposed to fit the person, or why alter them at all.
en.editorNote: For the day you finally buy something comfortable instead of something impressive.
variations: Letting the clothes adjust to you is its own kind of growing up.
Your definition of "fits" changes, which means you did too.

items.sourceNote: 島讀河溪「石頭的觀察」單元說明溪石表面藻類、日照與水位如何改變石頭；取其「同一塊石頭兩面完全不同」的觀察，改寫成整段黃昏降溫的過程

zh-tw.content:
午後的石頭上面還留著曬了一整天的溫度，靠水那面卻是冷的，手掌從上摸到下，像摸過兩個季節。
坐久一點，對岸的樹影會慢慢爬過來，先蓋住鞋尖，再蓋住膝蓋。
水一直在同一塊凸起的地方翻過去，那個聲音從頭到尾沒有變過。
等到整塊石頭都涼下來，天邊那條橘色也差不多要收了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種週末不想安排行程、只想找個地方坐到天黑的朋友。
variations: 同一塊石頭，上面是熱的，下面是冷的，兩邊都算數。
樹影會自己爬過來，不用你伸手去拉。

en.content:
The top of the rock still holds the whole afternoon's heat, while the side facing the water is cold; run your palm down it and you cross two seasons.
Sit long enough and the shade from the far bank comes to you, over your shoes first, then your knees.
The water keeps folding over the same raised stone, and that sound never once changes.
By the time the whole rock has gone cool, the orange strip at the horizon is packing up too.
en.editorNote: For a friend who wants no weekend plans, just somewhere to sit until dark.
variations: One rock, warm on top and cold underneath. Both readings are true.
The shade walks over to you. You don't have to go get it.

items.sourceNote: 科技大觀園〈溪流河川：川流不息的臺灣溪河生態〉提到台灣溪河短促流急、侵蝕旺盛、上游底質多為大型石塊；改寫成颱風後溪床重排、苔要重新長的情境

zh-tw.content:
颱風走了半個月才敢再去，水退到小腿以下，以前坐的那塊平石被沙埋掉一半。
上游滾下來的新石頭還沒長苔，白得刺眼，太陽一照，整片溪床都在反光。
苔會自己長回來，顏色也會再暗下去，只是這回長在別的位置上。
現在每一步都要重新找落腳點，鞋底磨到的地方跟去年不一樣了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合送給剛換工作、搬家或分手之後，正在重新認路的人。
variations: 新石頭反光是因為還沒長苔，不是因為它比較好。
位置換了，路就得重新踩一遍，這很合理。

en.content:
Half a month after the typhoon I finally went back; the water was below my calves and the flat rock I used to sit on was half buried in sand.
The new stones rolled down from upstream have no algae yet, so white it hurts, and the whole streambed throws the sun back at you.
The green will grow in again and the colour will darken again, only this time somewhere else.
Every step has to be worked out from scratch now, and the wear on my soles is in different places than last year.
en.editorNote: For someone re-learning the route after a new job, a move, or a breakup.
variations: The new stones are bright because nothing has grown on them yet, not because they're better.
The layout changed, so of course the walking has to be relearned.

items.sourceNote: 農業部食農教育資訊整合平臺「白露│秋分」介紹水氣遇冷凝結、空氣漸乾燥、一場秋雨一場寒；取其濕度轉換的節點，改寫成連日回潮後第一個晴天曬東西

zh-tw.content:
濕了十幾天之後，光第一天是斜的，從門縫進來一條，剛好落在地板那塊發霉的印子上。
把棉被、椅墊、球鞋一樣一樣搬到有太陽的地方，中午再去翻一次面。
傍晚收回屋裡的時候，布料是燙的，手按下去會慢慢彈回來。
夜裡躺平，鼻子聞到的味道跟前一天已經不同。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在連日陰雨終於放晴那天，發給一起被悶了好幾天的家人或室友。
variations: 曬過的棉被會回彈，這件事沒有道理不相信。
味道換了，就代表這幾天真的過去了。

en.content:
After a dozen damp days the light comes back slanted, one strip through the door gap, landing exactly on the mildew mark on the floor.
Quilt, chair cushion, running shoes, carried out one at a time into the sun, then flipped again at noon.
Bringing them in at dusk, the fabric is hot, and where you press it the shape rises back slowly.
Lying down that night, what your nose picks up is not what it picked up yesterday.
en.editorNote: To send on the first clear day after a long wet stretch, to whoever was shut in with you.
variations: Sun-dried fabric springs back. There's no reason not to trust that.
The smell changed, which means those days are actually over.

items.sourceNote: 環境資訊中心〈水波的律動 清涼水下的秘密〉說明水面波紋反射散射陽光、降低水溫；取「水面反光」的物理現象，改寫成雷陣雨前後的光線與氣味變化

zh-tw.content:
遠方那片雲壓過來的時候，風先轉向，一整排樹葉翻成背面的灰白。
接著氣味變了，柏油被打濕的那種腥味先到，雨才到。
屋簷底下站的人越來越多，沒有人講話，都朝同一邊看。
半小時後雨收了，光從雲的裂縫斜插下來，地上的水窪一格一格亮起來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在午後突然下大雨、對方傳訊說被困住的時候回一句。
variations: 樹葉翻白的時候，還有半小時可以慢慢走。
雨停了才會發現，地上多了那麼多會反光的東西。

en.content:
When that cloud leans in from the far side, the wind turns first, and a whole row of leaves flips to its pale grey underside.
Then the smell changes: wet asphalt arrives before the rain does.
More and more people gather under the eaves, nobody speaking, all facing the same way.
Half an hour later it stops, light drops in through a split in the cloud, and the puddles light up one panel at a time.
en.editorNote: A reply for when someone texts that they're stuck somewhere in a sudden downpour.
variations: When the leaves flip pale, you still have half an hour to walk it slowly.
Only after the rain do you notice how many things on the ground can shine.
